nsDocs.math: Standard Lua 5.1 math functions that this game's stripped runtime was missing, patched back in by lua-bridge. ADDITIVE -- the engine's own math.floor/abs/max/min and its separate math.randf() are untouched, so this list is not the whole of math.
nsDocs.TCP: A tiny outbound TCP helper added by lua-bridge. Loopback destinations only, by design.

AddInfraction.doc: Ai.AddInfraction(uCharacterGuid, uFactionGuid, nAmount) adds to a running "infraction" tally a character has against a faction, presumably feeding into relation decay.

AddSubject.doc: Ai.AddSubject(uGuid) registers an object with the AI subject-tracking system. Confirmed called when a player's character joins the game (resident/mrxplayer.lua).

Anchor.doc: Ai.Anchor({AIGuid = uGuid, AnchorRadius = n, ...}) pins a subject to its current position/area; AnchorRadius = 0 appears to mean it won't wander at all.

DefaultGoal.doc: Ai.DefaultGoal(tParameters) has no direct confirmed call sites, but resident/mrxai.lua wraps it 1:1 with Ai.Goal's calling convention (same table shape, same hibernation-gating), so it's inferred-by-analogy to share Goal's table shape rather than independently confirmed.

Deliver.doc: Ai.Deliver(uDriverGuid, nX, nY, nZ, nDropHeight, bCareless) commands a helicopter's AI driver to cargo-drop at a coordinate; nDropHeight sets drop altitude and bCareless likely relaxes precision/safety checks.

Deploy.doc: Ai.Deploy({Vehicle = uGuid, Role = sRole, Force = bForce, ...}) deploys/ejects occupants from a vehicle under AI control, e.g. Role = "Passenger", Force = true, MaintainRotorSpeed = true. Wrapped by resident/mrxai.lua with the same hibernation-gating as Goal.
Deploy.gotcha: Takes {Vehicle=, Role="Passenger", Force=} -- its argument table is not interchangeable with Ai.Goal's or Ai.Role's, and passing the wrong shape fails without an error.

Enable.doc: Ai.Enable(uGuid, bEnabled) toggles whether the AI system drives a given object at all. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua and resident/mrxutil.lua.

GetFactionGuid.doc: Ai.GetFactionGuid(uGuid) resolves an individual subject's owning faction guid, for use with GetRelation/SetRelation/etc.

GetFeeling.doc: Ai.GetFeeling(uGuidA, uGuidB) returns a numeric per-pair "feeling" value between two subjects, distinct from faction-level GetRelation (appears to be per-individual). At least one caller (resident/mrxfollow.lua) treats negative values as hostile.

GetRelation.doc: Ai.GetRelation(uGuidA, uGuidB) returns a numeric faction relation value (roughly -100 to 100) between two faction/subject guids. This is the literal primitive underneath MrxFactionManager's GetRelation wrapper; calling it directly bypasses that manager's HUD-meter and net-sync bookkeeping.

GetState.doc: Ai.GetState({AIGuid = uGuid, State = sStateName}) reads a named AI state flag for a subject (e.g. "NoCapture"). Table-shaped call, mirrors SetState's argument shape.

Goal.doc: Ai.Goal({AIGuid = uGuid, Goal = sGoalName, Target = ..., Priority = sPriority, ...}) issues a one-shot AI task (e.g. "PathMove") to a subject. Confirmed table keys: AIGuid, Goal, Target, Priority ("lowPri"/"hiPri"), Mode ("Oneway"), Start ("Nearest"), Haste, Callback, CallbackData. Returns a handle that can later be passed to RemoveGoal; the full set of valid Goal names/keys isn't enumerated anywhere in the corpus.
Goal.gotcha: A raw XYZ destination goes in `Location` (a plain {x,y,z} table), not `Position` and not `Target` (which takes a guid) -- and `Role` is NOT an Ai.Goal key at all. Worse, Goal="MoveToPos" with a Location silently returns nil for any ON-FOOT HUMAN regardless of distance (confirmed live; the corpus only ever uses it on a vehicle driver) -- use Goal="MoveTo" against a real object guid, spawning a TinyGeometry anchor at the destination if you need one.

LivingWorld.example: Ai.LivingWorld({ AIGuid = uGuid, Attrib = "LivingWorldBehaviour", State = false })
LivingWorld.doc: Ai.LivingWorld({AIGuid = uGuid, Attrib = sAttribName, State = ...}) enables/disables the ambient "living world" behavior layer for a subject, typically disabled (State = false) before scripting custom behavior like Follow on top.

RemoveExclusionZone.doc: Ai.RemoveExclusionZone() clears whatever AI exclusion zone is currently active; confirmed called with zero arguments. The counterpart SetExclusionZone has no confirmed call sites.

RemoveGoal.doc: Cancels a goal by handle. Confirmed in two shapes: Ai.RemoveGoal({AIGuid = uGuid, Handle = hHandle}) and positional Ai.RemoveGoal(uGuid, hHandle); both forms coexist in shipped scripts and which one a given engine build expects isn't resolvable from source alone.

RemoveSubject.doc: Ai.RemoveSubject(uGuid) unregisters a subject from the AI system; the confirmed counterpart to AddSubject, called on character teardown (resident/mrxplayer.lua).

Role.doc: Ai.Role({AIGuid = uGuid, Role = sRoleName, ...}) assigns a standing behavioral role (e.g. "Follow", "Idle") to a subject, as opposed to Goal's one-shot tasks; returns a handle. Follow example includes Target, MinDistance, MaxDistance, MoveDistance, Priority, HardPriority, Callback, CallbackData.
Role.gotcha: "Follow" is a ROLE, not a Goal -- Ai.Goal{Goal="Follow"} is wrong and the confirmed recipe is Ai.Role{Role="Follow", Target=...}. Ai.Goal / Ai.Role / Ai.Deploy argument tables are not interchangeable; mixing them is the most common way AI code fails silently.

SetFeeling.doc: Ai.SetFeeling(uGuidA, uGuidB, nValue) sets the per-pair feeling value; confirmed used to neutralize hostility (set to 100) before starting a scripted "Follow" role.

SetHaste.doc: Ai.SetHaste(uGuid, nHaste) is a numeric multiplier controlling how urgently/fast a driven subject moves; 1 appears to be normal/default speed.

SetInfractionMultiplier.doc: Ai.SetInfractionMultiplier(uFactionGuid, nMultiplier) scales infraction accrual for a faction: 0 suppresses it, 1 is normal, fractional values (e.g. 0.2) soften it during scripted sequences.

SetLaneActive.doc: Ai.SetLaneActive(uRoadGuid, nLaneIndex, bActive) enables/disables a specific numbered lane on a road object for traffic spawning/routing.

SetPriorityTarget.doc: Ai.SetPriorityTarget(uGuid) marks a subject as the priority target for hostile AI.

SetRelation.doc: Ai.SetRelation(uGuidA, uGuidB, nRelation) sets the numeric faction relation between two guids, e.g. Ai.SetRelation(uFactionA, uFactionB, -100). Literal primitive underneath MrxFactionManager's SetRelation; direct calls skip its mutability checks and HUD/net-sync side effects.

SetState.example: Ai.SetState({ AIGuid = uCarmona, State = "Vip", Value = true })
SetState.doc: Ai.SetState({AIGuid = uGuid, State = sStateName, Value = ...}) sets a named AI state flag on a subject, e.g. State = "Pacifist", Value = true. Confirmed across several resident/ and vz/ scripts.

Squad.doc: Ai.Squad({SquadGuid = uSquad, Action = sAction, ...}) performs squad-level operations. Confirmed Action "GetUnits" returns a table of unit guids belonging to the squad; other actions build squads from scratch but their keys are unconfirmed.

TestDropZone.doc: Ai.TestDropZone({Callback = fCallback, Location = {x,y,z}, InnerRadius, InnerHeightTolerance, OuterRadius, OuterHeightTolerance, HeightMax, SearchRadius, Water = bAllowWater}) tests for a valid helicopter landing/drop spot. Returns a boolean; false means no valid spot found, and callers respond with fCallback(false, "noland"). The best-documented table-shaped call in the namespace, used identically across mrxgunship, mrxsupportdesignator, mrxtankbuster, and pursuitcopter.

TweakAttachedSpawners.doc: Ai.TweakAttachedSpawners(uBuildingGuid, {SpawnerState = "on"/"off", SecondsPerCycle = n, SpawnList = sList, ...}) adjusts all AI spawners attached to a building/object. Very common in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua, resident/outpost.lua, and vz/ mission scripts.

TweakAttachedSpawnersInGroup.doc: Ai.TweakAttachedSpawnersInGroup(uBuildingGuid, sGroupName, {SpawnerState = ..., ...}) is the same as TweakAttachedSpawners but scoped to spawners tagged with a group name ("Ground", "Balcony", "Rooftop") instead of all spawners on the object.

Admire.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a manufactured AI subject: runs with no error and no crash, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot. Arguments are unconfirmed.
Admire.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies. Likely needs an engaged AI context (traffic, hostiles, other subjects) that the test spot did not provide.

ChangeRelation.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Given the confirmed Ai.GetRelation/Ai.SetRelation pair it is presumably a relative/delta adjustment rather than an absolute set, but that is a naming-based guess.

EveryoneOut.doc: Forces all occupants out of a vehicle. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) by reading Vehicle.GetDriver before and after the call: a real pilot guid became nil.
EveryoneOut.gotcha: Takes the vehicle's own guid, not a rider/pilot guid -- the opposite convention from Ai.HeliLand and Ai.Deliver, which want the pilot.

GetAttrib.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably the getter counterpart of the Attrib field seen in Ai.LivingWorld, but that pairing is inferred from naming only.

GetPerceivability.doc: Returns a subject's perceivability as two numbers -- a current value and a floor (e.g. 90, 5) -- read as a stealth/detectability rating and its minimum. Confirmed live (2026-07-22); read-only and safe to probe blind.
GetPerceivability.gotcha: Returns two values, not one. Unlike Ai.GetSubjectData it does answer for AI-controlled subjects, not just the player character.

GetSubjectData.doc: Returns the AI system's live threat/awareness tally for a subject as a table of {TotalAware, Attackers, TotalObservers, HostileObservers, HostileAware}. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) on the player character; read-only and safe to probe blind.
GetSubjectData.gotcha: Only the player character appears to be a tracked awareness subject -- probed against an AI-controlled helicopter pilot it returned nothing, where Ai.GetPerceivability returned real data for the same subject.

GoIn.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a subject guid and a target guid: executes cleanly, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot.
GoIn.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies.

HeliLand.doc: Commands a helicopter's AI pilot to descend and land. Confirmed live (2026-07-22): a test helicopter's Y position went from 7.5 down to ground level (-27.5) over roughly six seconds after the call.
HeliLand.gotcha: Takes the pilot/driver guid (the same convention as Ai.Deliver), not the vehicle's own guid. The descent takes several seconds -- the call returns long before the helicopter is down.

HeliTakeoff.doc: Intended counterpart to Ai.HeliLand, taking the pilot guid and optionally a destination coordinate. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executed cleanly but produced no observed ascent.
HeliTakeoff.gotcha: Inconclusive, not confirmed broken -- it likely needs a different trigger or prior AI state (e.g. already landed/idle) that the test spot did not provide.

RemoveAllSubjects.doc: Zero-argument call that live-probed cleanly (2026-07-22) but showed no observable effect at an isolated test spot holding only one manufactured subject.
RemoveAllSubjects.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- nothing confirms it actually clears the AI subject list.

Rest.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a manufactured AI subject: runs with no error, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot. Arguments are unconfirmed.
Rest.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies.

SetAttitude.doc: Takes a subject uGuid plus either an attitude string ("Hostile"/"Neutral"/"Friendly") or a raw number. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes cleanly, but showed no observable effect at an isolated test spot with nothing around to react.
SetAttitude.gotcha: MrxFactionManager builds its own attitude-label system entirely on Ai.GetRelation numeric thresholds and never calls this anywhere in the corpus -- whether Ai.SetAttitude overlaps with or bypasses that resident-side system is unconfirmed.

SetDriveThroughMassRatio.doc: Takes a single numeric ratio. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes cleanly with no observable effect at an isolated test spot, so what the ratio actually controls is unconfirmed.
SetDriveThroughMassRatio.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- likely needs live traffic present to show any effect.

SetFacing.doc: Turns a subject to face a given heading; the wiki records two candidate shapes, Ai.SetFacing(uGuid, nAngle) and Ai.SetFacing(uGuid, nX, nY, nZ). Live-probed 2026-07-22 against a flying helicopter's pilot and a just-exited pilot on foot: executed without error but produced no yaw change either time.
SetFacing.gotcha: Most likely only turns an idle, AI-driven ground NPC in place -- a flying helicopter's own flight AI owns its heading, and a just-exited pilot may not be a valid facing target at all.

SetPerceivability.doc: Sets a subject's perceivability (stealth/detectability) value. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) as a real, reversible state change: driving a subject 90 -> 30 -> 90 and reading it back with Ai.GetPerceivability between steps showed the value actually moves.
SetPerceivability.gotcha: A third argument exists but its purpose is unconfirmed.

ShowObjectSpawners.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably a debug-visualization toggle given the name, but that is a guess.

Temp.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Usage is completely unconfirmed, including argument count.

ConeSpawn.doc: Spawns nCount ordnance objects of vTemplate in a cone of half-angle nConeAngleDeg degrees around a direction vector, used for cluster/shrapnel spread patterns. Modules commonly stack multiple calls with widening angles and counts (e.g. a 15deg/10 ring then a 30deg/20 ring) for a denser pattern; no return value is used.

EquipDesignator.doc: Equips a target-designator "weapon" on uOwner — the tool a player aims to call in a strike (laser/smoke/flare/satellite/beacon). sDesignationType is a per-instance string; fCallback/tCallbackArgs fire when designation completes (nil means fire-and-forget); bFireImmediately skips the aim step. Returns the equipped weapon's guid.

Flyby.example: Airstrike.Flyby(tTemplates[sFaction], x - 50, z + 300, x, z, y + 100, 40)
Flyby.doc: Spawns a delivery aircraft (vDeliveryVehicle template string or instance field) that flies from a start point to an end point and invokes fDropCallback at the drop point, where the caller then spawns the actual ordnance. Argument order is two XZ pairs then Y — (startX, startZ, endX, endZ, Y, speed), not XYZ triples; callback/args are optional and speeds seen range 50-200. Returns the spawned jet's guid; this is the most-used call in the namespace after the two spawners.

SpawnCarpetBombLine.doc: Drops one row of a carpet-bomb pattern along nHeading and returns the next row's start XZ coordinates so the caller can loop to place successive rows. Only one confirmed call site exists, so the exact tail arguments (a nil 6th arg, then spacing and per-row count) are less certain than for higher-traffic calls.

SpawnDirectedObject.doc: Spawns a directed effect/particle object (not ordnance), oriented along the given direction vector, used for oriented explosion/fireball FX. vTemplate here is a global_particle_* name rather than an ordnance-template string. Returns the spawned object's guid.

SpawnOrdnance.doc: Spawns a single ordnance object (bomb/missile/shell) at a position with a velocity; vTemplate is a named engine-side ordnance template string (e.g. "Gunship Shell"), not a Lua data structure. The tail of the argument list is inconsistent across real call sites (some pass "impact"/a distance as arg 8, others insert a target uGuid first), so match the specific call site you're modeling rather than assuming one fixed signature. Returns the spawned ordnance guid.

SpawnTargettedOrdnance.doc: Same shape as SpawnOrdnance but always takes an explicit uTarget guid, used for homing/guided ordnance (e.g. missiles) rather than ballistic ordnance (bombs/shells). Confirmed usage: Airstrike.SpawnTargettedOrdnance("Vehicle AT Missile", nSpawnX, nSpawnY, nSpawnZ, nVectorX*nSpeedScale, nSpeedScale, nVectorZ*nSpeedScale, uTarget, "impact", 1, nil, BombExplodes, {uBomb}).

SpawnPlaneNew.doc: Surfaced from a static luaL_Reg engine-binding dump rather than any call site; disassembly shows it reads only a string plus one number. Live-probed 2026-07-22 with both a Flyby-style 7-argument call and a simple (name, x, y, z) call -- neither spawned anything visible nor returned a guid.
SpawnPlaneNew.gotcha: Not a working plane spawner as currently understood, despite the name. Airstrike.Flyby remains the confirmed, working mechanism for spawning delivery aircraft.

GetTranslationForStanceAndAction.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by name to look up a translation/offset keyed by a stance and an action, but signature and even general behaviour are unconfirmed.

PlayFaceAnim.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by name to play a facial animation on a character; signature unconfirmed.
PlayFaceAnim.gotcha: Distinct from the already-confirmed animation functions on the Object namespace -- this lives on the separate native Animation table.

Begin.doc: Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin() opens a scoped atmosphere-override block with no arguments, paired with one or more SetValue(sKey, nValue) calls and closed by End(). Confirmed used identically in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua script to start a temporary bloom/lighting override for an airstrike effect.

ChangeLineRegionSetting.doc: Graphics.Atmosphere.ChangeLineRegionSetting(uRegionGuid, sSettingName) applies a named weather/atmosphere preset to a specific map region. Confirmed example: applying the "warzone" preset to region "rgn_atmo_caracas".

End.doc: Graphics.Atmosphere.End() closes the scoped atmosphere override opened by Begin(), restoring the prior values. Confirmed called with no arguments in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua script.

GetValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed SetValue, using the same string-key convention -- assumed, not confirmed.

SetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetHenyeyGreensteinConst.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus. Henyey-Greenstein is a standard atmospheric-scattering phase function, consistent with the other sky/scattering tuning parameters on this sub-table.

SetLightIntensity.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus.
SetLightIntensity.gotcha: Distinct from the confirmed SetValue("fLightIntensity", n) key -- a same-named setter and a SetValue key are two different routes, and only the SetValue form is confirmed in use.

SetValue.doc: Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue(sKey, nValue) sets a named atmosphere/bloom/lighting parameter by string key inside a Begin()/End() scope, e.g. SetValue("fBloomAmount", 0.75) or SetValue("fLightIntensity", 1.55). Confirmed keys include fAtmosphereForce, fAtmosphereLimit, several fBloom* keys, fLightIntensity, and fTimeRestore.

SetBlurRadius.doc: Graphics.Bloom.SetBlurRadius(n) sets the bloom blur radius. Confirmed called once at boot with 0.5 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua alongside the other post-process defaults.

SetMultiplier.doc: Graphics.Bloom.SetMultiplier(n) sets the bloom intensity multiplier. Confirmed called at boot with 0 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.

SetThreshold.doc: Graphics.Bloom.SetThreshold(n) sets the bloom brightness threshold. Confirmed called at boot with 0.775 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.

Blend.doc: Starts a timed blend into a new camera state: `Camera.Blend(uCameraGuid, nBlendTime [, bFlag])`. Confirmed in real scripts, used immediately before setting position/look-at/shot to transition smoothly into a new cinematic camera state.

GetYaw.doc: Returns the yaw of the camera at uCameraGuid. Confirmed in real scripts, e.g. `self.nHeading = Camera.GetYaw(Player.GetCamera(self:GetOwner()))`; the camera guid must first be obtained via Player.GetCamera.

Hold.doc: Holds the camera in place: `Camera.Hold(uCameraGuid, bHold, bFlag2 [, bFlag3])`. Confirmed in real scripts with two or three booleans, typically called right after SetLookAt/Blend during cinematics; the exact per-argument meaning beyond "hold in place" is unconfirmed.

RestoreFocusParams.doc: Graphics.Camera.RestoreFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nDuration) reverts a SetFocusParams depth-of-field override back to normal over the given duration. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.

RestoreFovParams.doc: Graphics.Camera.RestoreFovParams(nCameraIndex, nDuration) reverts a SetFovParams field-of-view override. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.

RestoreNearFar.doc: Graphics.Camera.RestoreNearFar(nCameraIndex) reverts a SetNearFar clip-plane override. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.

SetFocusParams.doc: Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nStartNear, nEndNear, nStartFar, nEndFar, nBlur, nDuration) blends a depth-of-field focus transition (near/far planes and blur) over a duration; used during hijack and turret-mount cinematics. This is Graphics.Camera, distinct from the top-level Camera namespace, and the camera index is confirmed as 0 at every call site.

SetFovParams.doc: Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams(nCameraIndex, nAngle, nDuration) blends the field-of-view angle to a new value over a duration. Confirmed used in hijack and briefing cinematics with camera index 0.

SetLookAt.doc: Aims the camera at a target, either raw coordinates `Camera.SetLookAt(uCameraGuid, nX, nY, nZ, bLookAtDirection [, bFlag])` or an object+hardpoint pair `Camera.SetLookAt(uCameraGuid, uObjectGuid, sHardpoint, bLookAtDirection [, bFlag])`. Confirmed with both forms in `resident/mrxbriefing.lua`, and with a simpler object+hardpoint call in `resident/mrxactionhijack.lua` (e.g. aiming at bone_chest during a hijack-fail cinematic).
SetLookAt.gotcha: This is the call that ENABLES Camera.SetPosition -- with no SetLookAt target ever set, SetPosition is a silent no-op. Even a static target that is never repositioned is enough to unblock it.

SetNearFar.doc: Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar(nCameraIndex, nNear, nFar, nUnknown) directly sets the near/far clip planes, as opposed to SetFocusParams' blended depth-of-field near/far. The trailing 4th argument is 0 at every confirmed call site; its meaning is unconfirmed.

SetPitch.doc: Sets the camera's pitch to a numeric value: `Camera.SetPitch(uCameraGuid, nPitch)`. Confirmed in real scripts, e.g. `Camera.SetPitch(uCamera, 0.302)` paired right after `Camera.SetYaw(uCamera, 0)` during a teleport-recovery sequence.

SetPosition.doc: Positions the camera, in either a plain-coordinates form `Camera.SetPosition(uCameraGuid, nX, nY, nZ [, bFlag])` or an object+hardpoint form `Camera.SetPosition(uCameraGuid, uObjectGuid, sHardpoint [, bFlag])`. Both forms are confirmed side-by-side in `resident/mrxbriefing.lua` for cinematic camera setup; the trailing boolean's exact meaning is unconfirmed.
SetPosition.gotcha: Silently does NOTHING until an active Camera.SetLookAt binding exists -- not even a hardcoded, oversized test teleport moves the camera. Spawn a small anchor prop, SetLookAt the camera at it once, and SetPosition starts working immediately.

SetShot.doc: Selects a named scripted camera "shot" between two actors: `Camera.SetShot(uCameraGuid, sShotName, uBaseActor, uTargetActor [, bFlag])`. Confirmed in the cinematic-briefing system (`resident/mrxbriefing.lua`), used alongside Blend and Hold to frame e.g. an over-the-shoulder or two-shot between a base actor and a target actor.

SetYaw.doc: Sets the camera's yaw to a numeric value: `Camera.SetYaw(uCamera, nYaw)`. Confirmed with literal values like 0 and 80 in real scripts (e.g. teleport-recovery and player-camera reset code).

Shake.doc: Triggers a named screen-shake effect: `Camera.Shake(uCameraGuid, sShakeName, uSourceGuid, nAmplitude, nDuration)`. Confirmed with presets `"ShakeCameraMedium"`, `"ShakeCameraConstantlyRandom"`, and a matching stop call using `"StopShakeCameraConstantly"`; the shake name selects an engine-defined preset not present in the decompiled Lua corpus. The camera guid is usually from Player.GetCamera(...), but one script instead passes StringToGuid("0x1") (possibly a fixed/broadcast camera handle, unconfirmed).

StopBlending.doc: Stops an in-progress camera blend: `Camera.StopBlending(uCameraGuid)`. Confirmed at one call site (`vz/vzacon001.lua`), notably guarded with an existence check (`if uCam and Camera.StopBlending then`) before calling.

Follow.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Arguments beyond the presumed leading camera guid are unconfirmed.

GetFOV.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; usage unconfirmed. Takes the per-player camera guid from Player.GetCamera(uPlayerGuid), like the rest of this namespace.
GetFOV.gotcha: Do not confuse with Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams -- that is a different, confirmed-in-use function on the separate Graphics.Camera sub-table, which shares the name Camera and nothing else.

GetPitch.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Camera.SetPitch.

SetFOV.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; usage unconfirmed. Still flagged as needing a dedicated live-probe pass with an active cinematic mode running, not attempted as of 2026-07-22.
SetFOV.gotcha: Do not confuse with Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams on the separate Graphics.Camera sub-table -- same-sounding name, different table.

SetLimit.doc: Graphics.Contrast.SetLimit(n) sets the contrast limit for post-processing. Confirmed called at boot with 0.1 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.

SetMultiplier.doc: Graphics.Contrast.SetMultiplier(n) sets the contrast multiplier for post-processing. Confirmed called at boot with 1.5 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.

CameraFade.doc: Graphics.Effect.CameraFade(nAmount) triggers a full-screen fade-to-black/fade-in effect keyed by a 0/1 amount, not tied to a specific camera guid. Confirmed called with 0 and 1 at the start/end of a hijack cinematic.

Create.doc: Registers `callback` to run once when an event of `eventType` occurs, with a filter/parameter table whose shape depends entirely on the event type (e.g. ObjectDeath wants {targetGuid}, ObjectProximity wants {guidA, guidB, cmp, distance, bool, bool}). Returns a handle usable with Event.Delete to unregister. By far the most common event call in the codebase, used hundreds of times.
Create.gotcha: Event.Create(Event.TimerRelative, {sec}, fn) fires exactly ONCE -- fn must re-arm its own next call, and that re-arm must be the FIRST line of the callback: put it after the per-tick work and one uncaught error permanently kills the whole timer chain (the confirmed root cause of a tool that "never turned on"). The timer is also gated on SIMULATION time, so it stops firing entirely while the world is paused, e.g. whenever the PDA is open.

CreatePersistent.doc: Same call shape as Event.Create (eventType, {args}, callback, {callbackArgs}) plus an optional 5th boolean argument (bImmortalEvents). Used for events that should keep listening across multiple occurrences (e.g. repeated health-drop tracking, driver enter/exit) rather than a single fire-and-forget; the exact semantic difference from Create (repeat-fire vs. surviving something Create doesn't) is not confirmed from source.

Delete.doc: Unregisters an event previously registered via Event.Create or Event.CreatePersistent, given the handle it returned. Used pervasively for cleanup/teardown — store the handle and delete it when the listening context goes away to avoid stale callbacks firing later.
Delete.gotcha: The only way to unregister an Event.Create handle -- there is no clear-all native, so an event handle you drop on the floor stays live for the rest of the session. A self-rescheduling loop started from a re-run OnKey script leaks a whole extra loop per keypress unless you supersede it deliberately.

Post.doc: Broadcasts a custom named event: takes a string name (not a numeric Event.* constant) plus a data table, e.g. Event.Post("SurvivalMode", {uGuid}). Appears to be a separate custom-broadcast mechanism from the numeric Event.ScriptEvent ID; no confirmed call site shows Event.ScriptEvent listeners receiving Post-ed names, so the exact delivery relationship between the two is unconfirmed.

GetShadowBaseDistance.doc: Graphics.GetShadowBaseDistance() returns the current shadow draw distance with no arguments. Used to save off the current value before temporarily overriding it with SetShadowBaseDistance, then restoring it afterward.

InitTinyGeometry.doc: Graphics.InitTinyGeometry() takes no arguments; confirmed called once in resident/mrxtaskmission.lua. Presumably initializes a small/LOD geometry render pass, though exact behavior beyond the call site is unconfirmed.

SetBoundaryEffect.doc: Graphics.SetBoundaryEffect(nOpacity) controls the visual "boundary" (map edge / no-go zone) overlay effect opacity. Confirmed called with values like 0 and 0.25.

SetGamma.doc: Graphics.SetGamma(nMin, nMax, nGamma) sets the screen gamma range. Confirmed called identically at boot in shell/shellbootstrap.lua and resident/gamebootstrap.lua as Graphics.SetGamma(0, 0.8, 1).

SetShadowBaseDistance.doc: Graphics.SetShadowBaseDistance(nDistance) sets the shadow draw distance. Confirmed set to small values (2 during cinematic briefings, 10 elsewhere) and restored afterward, suggesting nDistance is a multiplier/scale rather than raw world units.

ReloadShaders.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name strongly suggests a dev/debug shader-hotreload utility.

SetNumFrameSync.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name suggests a frame-sync/vsync-count control; arguments unconfirmed.

SetScreenRatio.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to Graphics.GetScreenRatio.

ShowTinyGeometryObject.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed companion to the confirmed Graphics.InitTinyGeometry.

SetThreshold.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably an anti-aliasing edge-detection threshold.

Begin.doc: Opens a scoped atmosphere-override block, with no arguments. Confirmed in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua file as the opener for a Begin() / SetValue(sKey, nValue) / End() sequence that temporarily forces bloom and lighting for the duration of an airstrike effect.
Begin.gotcha: Must be paired with Graphics.Atmosphere.End() -- SetValue calls only apply inside the block.

ChangeLineRegionSetting.doc: Applies a named weather/atmosphere preset to a specific map region. Confirmed in vz/allcon003.lua: ChangeLineRegionSetting(Pg.GetGuidByName("rgn_atmo_caracas"), "warzone") -- reach for it to swap a region's mood for a mission beat.

End.doc: Closes the scoped override opened by Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin(), with no arguments. Confirmed in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua file.

GetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.GetValue, same string-key convention.

GetCurrentSetting.doc: Exists per the live enumeration; not individually traced against the decompiled corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to ChangeLineRegionSetting/Change.

GetIntValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the integer-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.GetValue.

GetLineRegionSetting.doc: Exists per the live enumeration; not individually traced against the decompiled corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed ChangeLineRegionSetting.

GetValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed SetValue, using the same string-key convention -- assumed, not confirmed.

SetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetHenyeyGreensteinConst.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus. Henyey-Greenstein is a standard atmospheric-scattering phase function, consistent with the other sky/scattering tuning parameters on this sub-table.

SetIntValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the integer-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetLightIntensity.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus.
SetLightIntensity.gotcha: Distinct from the confirmed SetValue("fLightIntensity", n) key -- a same-named setter and a SetValue key are two different routes, and only the SetValue form is confirmed in use.

SetValue.doc: Sets one named atmosphere/bloom parameter inside a Begin()/End() block. Confirmed extensively in resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua, e.g. SetValue("fBloomAmount", 0.75), SetValue("fAtmosphereLimit", 200), SetValue("fLightIntensity", 1.55). Confirmed keys: fAtmosphereForce, fAtmosphereLimit, fBloomAdaptiveLuminancePercent, fBloomAdaptiveLuminanceScale, fBloomAmount, fBloomBlurRadius, fBloomContastLimit, fBloomContastMultiplier, fBloomMultiplier, fBloomTargetLuminance, fBloomThreshold, fLightIntensity, fTimeRestore.
SetValue.gotcha: Two confirmed key names are misspelled in the engine and must be passed exactly as-is: fBloomContastLimit and fBloomContastMultiplier (sic -- no 'r' in 'Contrast').

SetAdaptiveLuminancePercent.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomAdaptiveLuminancePercent key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetAdaptiveLuminanceScale.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomAdaptiveLuminanceScale key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetBlurRadius.doc: Sets the bloom blur radius. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called once at boot with 0.5 alongside the other post-process defaults.

SetMultiplier.doc: Sets the bloom multiplier. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.

SetTargetLuminance.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomTargetLuminance key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

SetThreshold.doc: Sets the bloom brightness threshold. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.775.

RestoreFocusParams.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams depth-of-field override over the given duration. Confirmed in resident/emplaced.lua, resident/mrxactionhijack.lua, resident/mrxbriefing.lua and vz/xQ!L.lua, always with camera index 0.

RestoreFovParams.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams override over the given duration. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua and vz/xQ!L.lua, called as RestoreFovParams(0, 1).

RestoreNearFar.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar override. Confirmed in vz/wifpmcinterior.lua, vz/xQ!L.lua and resident/mrxhq.lua, all called as RestoreNearFar(0).

SetFocusParams.doc: Controls the depth-of-field blur transition -- near and far focus planes blending over a duration. Confirmed with 7 arguments during hijack and turret-mount cinematics (resident/mrxactionhijack.lua, resident/emplaced.lua); one call site uses only 6.
SetFocusParams.sig: Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nStartNear, nEndNear, nStartFar, nEndFar, nBlur, nDuration)
SetFocusParams.gotcha: The first argument is a numeric camera index (0 at every call site seen), not a uGuid -- Graphics.Camera is a different table from the top-level Camera namespace, which does take a guid.

SetFovParams.doc: Blends the render camera's field-of-view angle to a new value over a duration. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua and resident/mrxbriefing.lua; pair with RestoreFovParams to undo.
SetFovParams.gotcha: This is Graphics.Camera, a DIFFERENT native table from the Camera.* chase-cam family it sits next to -- and it takes a player INDEX, not a camera guid. Confirmed cross-namespace footgun: the two share only a name.

SetLodParams.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to control level-of-detail distance thresholds, by analogy with the sibling near/far/focus/FOV setters.

SetNearFar.doc: Sets the render camera's near/far clip planes directly, as opposed to SetFocusParams' blended depth-of-field planes. Confirmed in vz/wifpmcinterior.lua and resident/mrxhq.lua, e.g. SetNearFar(0, 0.3, 500, 0) -- reach for it when an interior or a custom draw distance needs the far plane pulled in.
SetNearFar.gotcha: The trailing 4th argument is 0 at every call site and its meaning is unconfirmed. First argument is a camera index, not a guid.

SetLimit.doc: Sets the post-process contrast limit. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.1.

SetMultiplier.doc: Sets the post-process contrast multiplier. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 1.5.

AmbientSides.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed paired with Graphics.Effect.AmbientTop for directional ambient-lighting tuning.

CameraFade.doc: Full-screen fade-to-black/fade-in keyed by a 0/1 amount. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua at the start and end of a hijack cinematic.
CameraFade.gotcha: Not tied to a specific camera guid -- it is a global screen effect, unlike the per-camera calls on the top-level Camera namespace.

Extinguish.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to Graphics.FuelTrail.Ignite.

Ignite.doc: Zero call sites anywhere in the decompiled corpus, including the vehicle fuel-tank damage code in resident/mrxpmc.lua. The name strongly suggests it starts a leaking-fuel particle trail, but no in-repo evidence connects it to that or any other system.
Ignite.gotcha: Argument shapes are completely unknown for the whole Graphics.FuelTrail sub-table -- test carefully in-game before relying on it.

SetGradient.doc: Takes 10 numeric arguments; confirmed called twice back-to-back at boot in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, presumably defining a two-stop colour-grading/tone curve for shadow and highlight ranges.
SetGradient.sig: Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient(n1, n2, n3, n4, n5, n6, n7, n8, n9, n10)
SetGradient.gotcha: The exact per-argument meaning is not confirmed -- only that 10 numbers are passed and that the two boot calls cover different input ranges (0-128 and 128-255).

ControllerInUse.doc: Returns whether a controller (vs mouse/keyboard) is currently in use, no arguments. Guard-checked like IsXboxController; confirmed used to branch tutorial prompt phrasing between mouse/keyboard and controller in vzacon001.lua and wift tutorial scripts.

DoSigninCheck.doc: Runs the platform sign-in check with no arguments; confirmed called as part of the shell/platform-signin flow in mrxguishell.lua.

EnablePlayerMarkers.doc: Toggles rendering of player markers on screen (bEnabled boolean). Confirmed used as Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers(false)/(true) in mrxbriefing.lua to hide/show player markers during cutscenes and briefings.

FindGuiLocation.doc: Gui.FindGuiLocation(uOwnerOrPlayerGuid, uTargetGuid) returns nX1, nY1, nX2, nY2 — a screen-space bounding box (two corner points) for a world object, confirmed used to anchor UI overlays/tutorial callouts (mrxguisatellite.lua, mrxguitutorial.lua).

GetLanguageName.doc: Returns the current localization language name as a string, no arguments. Confirmed used in mrxsoundbanks.lua (local sLanguage = Gui.GetLanguageName()) to pick the correct localized sound bank.

GetReticlePosition.doc: Gui.GetReticlePosition(uOwnerGuid) returns nX, nY: 2D screen-space coordinates of the reticle for the given owner (e.g. oWidget:GetOwner()), confirmed with 5 call sites in mrxguihudreticle.lua. Distinct from Player.GetTargetUnderReticle, which returns the 3D world position/guid of whatever the reticle is aimed at; the two are complementary, not duplicates.

IsPdaOnSelect.doc: Returns a boolean with no arguments; confirmed guard-checked before use (if Gui.IsPdaOnSelect and Gui.IsPdaOnSelect() then) in mrxguipda.lua.

IsXboxController.doc: Returns whether an Xbox controller is in use, no arguments. Always guard-checked in real scripts (if Gui.IsXboxController and Gui.IsXboxController() then), suggesting it may not exist on all platform builds.

LoadFont.doc: Loads a font by name for HUD use, taking a single font-name string. Confirmed e.g. Gui.LoadFont("fanfare_36") in mrxguihudmessage.lua.

LoadTexture.doc: Loads a texture by name for HUD use (sTextureName [, sType]). Confirmed extensively, often with an explicit "texture" type string as the 2nd arg (e.g. 24 consecutive HUD-icon preload calls in mrxguihudactionhijack.lua), but also called with just the name elsewhere, so the 2nd argument is optional.

OnGlobalExit.doc: Called with no arguments as part of global game-exit teardown; confirmed in mrxstate.lua.

OnShellLoaded.doc: Called with no arguments as part of the shell-load lifecycle; confirmed guard-checked (if Gui.OnShellLoaded then Gui.OnShellLoaded() end) in mrxguishell.lua.

SetPickupMarkerSize.doc: Sets the on-screen size of pickup markers (nSize, bFlag). Confirmed real usage passes the same numeric size with the boolean flag flipped back-to-back (e.g. SetPickupMarkerSize(18, false) then (18, true) in hero.lua); the exact meaning of the flag is unconfirmed, possibly a near/far or friendly/enemy marker-set selector.

SetPickupMarkerVisibleDistance.doc: Sets the visible distance for pickup markers (nDistance, bFlag). Confirmed as Gui.SetPickupMarkerVisibleDistance(20, false) in hero.lua, at the same call site as SetPickupMarkerSize, run inside a 3-second delayed Event.TimerRelative block during survival-mode setup.

ShowLoadingHints.doc: Toggles the loading-screen hint text on/off (bShow boolean). Confirmed always guard-checked first in real scripts, e.g. if Gui.ShowLoadingHints then Gui.ShowLoadingHints(false) end in mrxgui.lua.

EnableFactionMarkers.doc: Toggles the faction marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

EnablePickupMarkers.doc: Toggles the pickup marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

EnableVehicleEntranceMarkers.doc: Toggles the vehicle-entrance marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

GetLanguageNum.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Gui) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed the numeric-ID counterpart to the confirmed Gui.GetLanguageName.

OutputToPIX.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Gui) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name suggests a PIX (graphics-debugger) event/marker output hook for dev builds.

_MarkerAdd.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Add.
_MarkerAdd.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Add instead. The 1:1 name correspondence is a well-supported hypothesis from two live pairs() dumps, not a confirmed engine-internals finding.

_MarkerAdd3D.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Add3D.
_MarkerAdd3D.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Add3D instead.

_MarkerAddDisc.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.AddDisc instead.

_MarkerAddOld.gotcha: Flagged as a naming mismatch rather than an assumed pairing: its exact relationship to Marker.AddBlip -- the one public Marker function with no equally-named _Marker* counterpart -- is unconfirmed.

_MarkerSetBlipLimit.gotcha: Not an exact name match to any public Marker function -- the pairing with Marker.SetGroupedBlipLimit is by closest function, not by name.
