Commence.doc: Shows the contact-card fanfare popup -- faction, title, name, job title, two phone fields and an email, with a display time and optional callback. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua; the full field list comes from the resident/mrxguiinterface.lua implementation.
Commence.sig: Hud.CardFanfare:Commence({sFaction=s, sTitle=s, sName=s, sJobTitle=s, sPhone1=s, sPhone2=s, sEmail=s, nDisplayTime=n, fCallback=fn, tCallbackData=t})

Commence.doc: Shows the new-contact fanfare popup. Confirmed in vz/meccon001.lua; the implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.fCallback and tArgs.tCallbackData.

Shows the standard event toast, keyed by an sType from the fanfare catalog plus the text to display. Confirmed across resident/mrxpmc.lua, resident/mrxunlockfanfare.lua and resident/mrxtaskjobverifyset.lua, and confirmed working by live testing -- the go-to call for a custom on-screen toast.
Commence.gotcha: The text field is vText; the implementation only normalises a legacy sText field into vText when vText is absent.

AddItem.doc: Adds one ledger item to a fanfare being built. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, called repeatedly between Hud.Fanfare:Create and Hud.Fanfare:Commence.

Commence.doc: Fires the fanfare that was built with Create/AddItem. Confirmed in vz/mecjob.lua as Hud.Fanfare:Commence({}); the implementation reads tArgs.nSlowdownDuration.

Create.doc: Opens a new ledger-style fanfare. Confirmed in vz/mecjob.lua and resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua as the first step of a Create -> AddItem -> Commence sequence.

Complete.doc: Job-completed fanfare. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take a table argument like its confirmed siblings.

Failed.doc: Job-failed fanfare. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take a table argument like its confirmed siblings.

AddMessage.doc: Queues an objective-style HUD message and returns a message-id table. Widely confirmed (resident/mrxguiinterface.lua's DisplayObjectiveMessage, resident/mrxsupport.lua, resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, several vz/ scripts); a minimal {sMessage = "..."} table works too.
AddMessage.sig: tMsgIds = Hud.MessageBox:AddMessage({sMessage=s, nPriority=n, nDuration=n, bClearBuffer=b, bAllowsAppends=b, fCallback=fn})
AddMessage.gotcha: Capture the returned id table -- it is what Hud.MessageBox:ModifyPendingMessage and RemovePendingMessage expect.

Clear.doc: Clears the message box. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, called with an empty table.

ModifyPendingMessage.doc: Rewrites a still-pending message in place, using the id table AddMessage returned, and returns a success boolean. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

RemovePendingMessage.doc: Removes a still-pending message. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take the same message-id table AddMessage returns, by analogy with ModifyPendingMessage.

ClearSlot.doc: Clears one numbered objective-tray slot. Extremely common in vz/ mission scripts, both as ClearSlot({vPlayer = nil, nSlot = 1}) and the shorter ClearSlot({nSlot = 1}).
ClearSlot.gotcha: The vPlayer field appears to be optional -- both forms occur in shipped scripts.

SetSlotToImage.doc: Puts an image in an objective-tray slot. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua alongside SetSlotToText in the same dispatch function; the exact field list was not fully confirmed.

SetSlotToText.doc: Sets the text shown in one of the small numbered objective-tray slots. Dozens of confirmed call sites across vz/ mission scripts -- the standard way to drive on-screen objective text.

SetSlotToWidget.doc: Puts a widget in an objective-tray slot. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed similar in shape to SetSlotToText/SetSlotToImage.

AddLineRegion.doc: Draws a line region (a boundary outline) on the radar from a pre-built region-parameter table. Confirmed in resident/factionzone.lua, resident/mrxguiinterface.lua and vz/wifvzboundary.lua.

AddObjective.doc: Adds a radar blip for an objective, with colour, size, texture, target guid and sort order. Confirmed extensively -- resident/blippable.lua's objective-marker class, mrxfactionmanager, mrxhq, mrxsupport, outpost, mrxtaskobjective and more.
AddObjective.sig: Hud.Radar:AddObjective({sName=s, nR=n, nG=n, nB=n, nWidth=n, nHeight=n, sTexture=s, uGuid=u, bSticky=b, bRotate=b, bOriented=b, nSortOrder=n, bDontNetSync=b})

AnimateObjectiveAlpha.doc: Animates an existing radar blip's alpha. Confirmed in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua and vz/oilcon002.lua with a table argument; the field list beyond a presumed name key was not pinned down.

AnimateObjectiveSize.doc: Pulses/animates an existing radar blip's size, e.g. AnimateObjectiveSize({sName = sBlipName}). Confirmed in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua, mrxparkinglotmanager, mrxtaskobjective and two vz/ scripts.

AnimateObjectiveSonar.doc: Plays the sonar-ping animation on a radar blip. Confirmed in resident/mrxfactionmanager.lua with a table argument.

RemoveLineRegion.doc: Removes a radar line region, most often as RemoveLineRegion({uGuid = uBoundary}). Confirmed in the same three files as Hud.Radar:AddLineRegion.

RemoveObjective.doc: Removes an objective blip by name. Confirmed widely alongside Hud.Radar:AddObjective.
RemoveObjective.gotcha: One shipped call site (vz/pmccon001.lua) passes a positional array shape, Hud.Radar:RemoveObjective({uDoor}), so the accepted shapes are not uniform.

UnanimateObjective.doc: Stops a blip animation. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed counterpart to the Animate* family.

UpdateObjective.doc: Updates an existing radar blip from a pre-built config table matching AddObjective's shape. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskobjective.lua.

Hide.doc: Hides the HUD resource counter. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua, called with an empty table.

SetCash.doc: Drives the cash readout in the HUD resource counter, with an optional reason string and increment for the change animation. Confirmed in resident/mrxpmc.lua's DisplayCash/DisplayResources.

SetFuel.doc: Drives the fuel readout, taking the current value, the max, and an optional increment. Confirmed in resident/mrxpmc.lua's DisplayResources.

SetSuppressed.doc: Hides or shows the cash and fuel readouts independently. Confirmed in resident/mrxstate.lua (both directions) and resident/mrxmissionflow.lua.

Show.doc: Shows the HUD resource counter for nDuration. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua as Show({nDuration = -1}).

AddItem.doc: Adds an item to the support fanfare. The implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.sTexture, sItemName, sFaction, sContactName and sBlipName.

Commence.doc: Fires the support fanfare built with Create/AddItem. Implemented in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

Create.doc: Opens a support fanfare. The implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.fCallback and tArgs.tCallbackData.

Commence.doc: Shows a two-line text fanfare with entrance, display and fade times plus an optional callback. No direct call site was found, but the field list is confirmed from the resident/mrxguiinterface.lua implementation.
Commence.sig: Hud.TextFanfare:Commence({sLine1=s, sLine2=s, nEntranceTime=n, nDisplayTime=n, nFadeTime=n, fCallback=fn, tCallbackData=t})

SetText.doc: The lowest-level entry point for a tutorial HUD message: SetText({vPlayer = Player.GetLocalPlayer(), sText = sMessage}) shows it, and calling again with sText = nil clears it. Confirmed in resident/mrxtutorialmanager.lua.
SetText.gotcha: Do not call it directly in a mod -- use MrxTutorialManager.ShowMessage/HideMessage, which additionally handles net-sync, duplicate suppression and identifier-based message ownership that this call bypasses.

ShowTutorialForObject.doc: Shows a tutorial prompt tied to an object. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed a table argument like the confirmed Hud.Tutorial:SetText.

ShowTutorialOnscreen.doc: Shows an on-screen tutorial prompt. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed a table argument like the confirmed Hud.Tutorial:SetText.

DisableWeapons.doc: Disables a character's weapons, given a character uGuid. Extremely common, always paired with EnableWeapons elsewhere in the same module.

DoAction.doc: Plays a named scripted action/pose on a character: Human.DoAction(uGuid, sActionName). Observed action names include "Cower", "Stand", "VerifyCamera", "shieldface", and "Proximity".

Drop.doc: Makes a character drop whatever it's carrying: Human.Drop(uGuid [, bFlag]). Always called right after Human.IsCarrying returns true; the optional second boolean argument's exact effect isn't confirmed.

EnableWeapons.doc: Re-enables a character's weapons, given a character uGuid. Counterpart to DisableWeapons.

ForceExitSeatNoSnap.doc: Forces a character out of a vehicle seat without the normal snap-to-ground/exit animation, given a character uGuid.

IsCarrying.doc: Returns whether a character is currently carrying something, given a character uGuid. Always checked immediately before a paired Human.Drop call in real scripts.

IsGrappling.doc: Returns whether a character is currently grappling, given a character uGuid. Always checked immediately before a paired Human.StopGrappling call in real scripts.

IsSwimming.doc: Returns whether a character is currently swimming, given a character uGuid. Used e.g. to decide whether a support drop should be treated as a water pickup; one call site guards the call defensively (if Human.IsSwimming and ...), suggesting the function's presence was historically treated as uncertain.

Knockdown.doc: Knocks a character down for a given numeric duration: Human.Knockdown(uGuid, nDuration), e.g. Human.Knockdown(uCharacter, 0.5).

PersistTransform.doc: Persists a character's current transform, given a character uGuid. Confirmed call sites but exact effect beyond the name isn't detailed.

PlayRawAnimation.example: Human.PlayRawAnimation(uGuid, sAnim, false, false, -1, true, true)
PlayRawAnimation.doc: Plays a raw named animation on a character with loop and blend-related flags: Human.PlayRawAnimation(uGuid, sAnimName, bLoop, bFlag2, nBlendTime, bFlag4 [, bFlag5]), optionally returning a success boolean. Exact meaning of the flags/blend-time beyond the animation name and loop flag is unconfirmed.

Scrub.doc: Called on a character uGuid immediately following a Drop/SetState("Upright","Idle") cleanup sequence; likely resets/clears transient character state, but the exact effect is not confirmed.

SetAllowCorpseCleanup.doc: Enables or disables corpse cleanup for a character: Human.SetAllowCorpseCleanup(uGuid, bAllow). One call site wraps the result in a debug print, implying it returns the previous state, though that's inferred rather than confirmed.

SetFireLock.doc: Locks or unlocks a character's ability to fire their weapon: Human.SetFireLock(uGuid, bLocked). Used to prevent/allow firing during a scripted shooting-gallery sequence.

SetJostleEnabled.doc: Toggles whether a character can be jostled, via a character uGuid and boolean: Human.SetJostleEnabled(uChar, bOn). Only one confirmed call site.

SetPreemptiveRagdoll.doc: Puts a character into a preemptive ragdoll state ahead of some scripted event, given a character uGuid. Used in hijack setup/failure paths alongside Knockdown and ForceExitSeatNoSnap.

SetState.doc: Sets a named state on a character along with a paired string value: Human.SetState(uGuid, sStateName, sAnimOrValue). Observed states: "InVehicle" (paired with an animation name), "Upright" (paired with "Idle"), and "Subdued" (paired with "Idle").

StopGrappling.doc: Stops a character's current grapple, given a character uGuid. Always called right after Human.IsGrappling returns true.

EquipWeapon.gotcha: This top-level form has ZERO real call sites anywhere in the decompiled corpus. The confirmed-working call is Human.Inventory.EquipWeapon(uChar, uWeapon).

DropWeapon.doc: Makes a character drop a specific weapon. Very common in real scripts, always with a character uGuid and a weapon uGuid.

EquipWeapon.doc: Swaps a character's currently-held weapon for a weapon uGuid previously fetched via GetPrimaryWeapon/GetSecondaryWeapon. Confirmed in resident/mrxshootinggallery.lua.

GetAllWeapons.doc: Returns a table of the weapon guids a character is carrying. Extremely common in real scripts (resident/hero.lua, resident/soldier.lua).
GetAllWeapons.gotcha: Some call sites pass a second boolean argument (e.g. in resident/mrxplayer.lua); its effect is unconfirmed.

GetPrimaryWeapon.doc: Returns the primary weapon uGuid for a character, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon(Player.GetLocalCharacter()). Confirmed in resident/mrxstatsmanager.lua.

GetSecondaryWeapon.doc: Returns the secondary weapon uGuid for a character. Confirmed in resident/mrxshootinggallery.lua.

ReloadAll.doc: Reloads all of a character's weapons. Confirmed in one real call site with a character uGuid and a boolean, vz/xQ!L.lua.

SetAllWeapons.doc: Sets a character's whole loadout from an array-style table of weapon uGuids, e.g. SetAllWeapons(uCharGuid, {uPrimary, uGrenade, uC4}) in resident/mrxplayer.lua.
SetAllWeapons.gotcha: Some vz/ scripts pass a single uGuid where the table is expected, so the full set of accepted argument shapes is not pinned down.

DropWeapon.doc: Drops a specific weapon from a character's inventory. Takes a character uGuid and a weapon uGuid: Human.Inventory.DropWeapon(uCharGuid, uWeaponGuid). Very common across mission scripts.

EquipWeapon.doc: Equips a previously-fetched weapon uGuid onto a character, swapping out whatever they're currently holding. Confirmed usage: Human.Inventory.EquipWeapon(uPlayer, uWeaponGuid), e.g. paired with GetPrimaryWeapon/GetSecondaryWeapon. This is the actually-used form; the top-level Human.EquipWeapon exists but has zero confirmed call sites.

GetAllWeapons.doc: Returns a table of weapon guids held by the given character uGuid. Extremely common; some call sites pass an additional boolean second argument whose effect is unconfirmed.

GetPrimaryWeapon.doc: Returns the primary weapon uGuid for a given character uGuid, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon(Player.GetLocalCharacter()).

GetSecondaryWeapon.doc: Returns the secondary weapon uGuid for a given character uGuid, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetSecondaryWeapon(uPlayer).

ReloadAll.doc: Reloads all of a character's weapons. Confirmed with a character uGuid and a boolean flag in one real call: Human.Inventory.ReloadAll(uCharacter, false); the boolean's exact meaning isn't confirmed.

SetAllWeapons.doc: Sets a character's full weapon loadout from an array-style table of weapon uGuids, e.g. Human.Inventory.SetAllWeapons(uCharGuid, {uPrimary, uGrenade, uC4}). Some call sites instead pass a single weapon uGuid in place of the table, so the full accepted argument shapes aren't fully pinned down.

DrawPath.doc: Junk.DrawPath(uPathGuid) draws/visualizes a path object. Confirmed in vz/meccon001.lua, called with a path GUID (resolved via Pg.GetGuidByName) immediately before passing that same GUID to Ai.Goal({Goal="PathMove", Target=uPath,...}) — reads as a debug/AI-path visualization aid with no mechanical gameplay effect.

FormatTime.doc: Junk.FormatTime(nTime [, bUseTenths]) formats a numeric time value into a display string. Confirmed used in resident/mrxtimer.lua and resident/mrxstatsmanager.lua feeding a displayed stats string; the optional second boolean argument appears to control whether tenths-of-a-second are included.

InstallToHDD.doc: Junk.InstallToHDD() takes no arguments. Confirmed in resident/mrxguishell.lua as the callback run when the player picks the "install to HDD" option in the console install-options menu; disc/HDD-install tooling, not gameplay-relevant.

IsInstallable.doc: Junk.IsInstallable() takes no arguments and returns a value used in a boolean context. Confirmed in mrxguishell.lua, called defensively as `if Junk.IsInstallable and Junk.IsInstallable() then` — part of the console install-menu plumbing.

UseExistingInstall.doc: Junk.UseExistingInstall() takes no arguments. Confirmed in the same mrxguishell.lua install-menu callback, invoked when the player selects "Use Existing HDD Install"; console install tooling, not gameplay-relevant.

ActivateAlarm.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; independently corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by a static luaL_Reg registration-table dump. Presumed a one-directional counterpart to Junk.ToggleAlarm.
ActivateAlarm.gotcha: resident/alarm.lua calls its own local AlarmActivated/AlarmDeactivated rather than this, so the relationship is inferred from naming only. The binding audit proves table membership, not argument shape.

CreateRegion.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; independently corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by the static luaL_Reg registration-table audit -- membership only, no argument shape recovered.

DescribeGuid.doc: The name strongly suggests a debug helper returning a human-readable description (type/name/state) for a uGuid, which would be directly useful for object-identification work.
DescribeGuid.gotcha: Unconfirmed and untested -- no call sites anywhere in the corpus. Treat it as a lead to probe live, not a documented API.

GetModelBBoxExtents.doc: Returns a model's bounding-box extents along each axis as three numbers (a boat measured 19.98, 18.74, 22.71). Confirmed live 2026-07-22 -- the way to size an object before placing or fitting something around it.
GetModelBBoxExtents.gotcha: Takes a uGuid, NOT a model/template name string -- easy to assume otherwise for a model-lookup function, since Pg.Spawn wants a name. The signature comes entirely from live probing; there are no call sites in the corpus.

SpawnHomingProjectile.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites; corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by the static luaL_Reg audit. The likeliest candidate for the mechanism behind AntiAir's homing missiles, since resident/antiair.lua never calls Airstrike anywhere.
SpawnHomingProjectile.gotcha: That AntiAir connection is inference from the name, not a confirmed call chain, and no argument shape was recovered.

SpawnWithModel.doc: Investigated in full as a possible additive-model-spawning route and confirmed a dead end -- see the wiki's dedicated writeup. No call sites in the corpus.
SpawnWithModel.gotcha: Not a working spawner as understood; do not build on it.

ToggleAlarm.doc: Toggles an alarm object -- the function that actually runs when a player interacts with an alarm. Confirmed in resident/alarm.lua, wired as the Event.ContextAction callback for the alarm object.
ToggleAlarm.gotcha: Genuinely gameplay-relevant despite living on the dev/debug-flavoured Junk namespace.

ClearKeyEvents.doc: Drops every buffered key event without returning it. An explicit reset point -- e.g. call it the instant a chat input opens, so whatever was being pressed beforehand does not leak in as the first characters typed.

GetKeyboardState.doc: Returns a 256-byte string, one byte per virtual-key code, high bit set if that key is down right now. Read one key with string.byte(s, vk + 1) >= 128. Backed by GetAsyncKeyState (physical, system-wide) -- deliberately NOT the Win32 call of the same name, which reflects the calling thread's message queue and can return stale data.
GetKeyboardState.gotcha: Returns a 256-byte string, not a table -- read one key with `string.byte(s, vk + 1) >= 128`. It takes numeric Windows VK codes, a completely different scheme from an OnKey script's `KEYVAL = "keyname"` string; the two are not interchangeable.

IsGameFocused.doc: Whether the foreground window belongs to the game's own process, by process-ID match rather than window-handle or style checks, so it stays correct under borderless/fullscreen/multi-window setups. The same check that gates PopKeyEvents, exposed so a script can branch on focus itself.

IsKeyDown.doc: Single-key predicate: wraps one GetAsyncKeyState and returns a plain boolean, for when you care about one key and would rather not index a 256-byte string yourself.
IsKeyDown.gotcha: NEVER call this per-key in a loop -- every framerate bug this project has hit in a custom menu, console or HUD came from exactly that, independently, more than once. Poll Loader.PopKeyEvents() plus one Loader.GetKeyboardState() snapshot ONCE per tick instead.

LoadVar.doc: Reads back a value saved with SaveVar, preserving its original type. Returns nil for a key that was never saved. New in lua-bridge v0.3.0.
LoadVar.gotcha: Returns nil for a key that was never saved -- and reads the same flat, mod-shared namespace Loader.SaveVar writes, so an unprefixed key can pick up another mod's value. Types survive the round trip (5 comes back as a number, not "5").

PopKeyEvents.doc: Returns a string of raw VK-code bytes, one per up-to-down edge since the last call, in press order. Filled by a ~60Hz C-side sampler into a 128-slot ring, so polling once a frame never misses a keystroke to timing the way hand-rolled edge detection over IsKeyDown snapshots does. Empty string when nothing was pressed. Focus-gated: keystrokes are dropped while the game is not the foreground window, so a chat box built on this cannot capture typing meant for another application.
PopKeyEvents.gotcha: An edge-triggered ring buffer with NO "still held" signal -- it reports up-to-down transitions only. It's also FOCUS-GATED: keystrokes are silently dropped whenever the game isn't the foreground window, by design.

Printf.doc: Appends a line to lua_loader_printf.log next to the .asi. The low-noise alternative to the engine's Debug.Printf, which stock game scripts fire thousands of times a frame. This is the logging call the wiki uses throughout, and what the IDE's Log & telemetry tab reads.
Printf.gotcha: Despite the name it does NOT do format substitution -- passing a format string and arguments printed a literal %s when tested against a running game. Build the string yourself with string.format first.

SaveVar.doc: Persists a number, string or boolean under sKey, surviving a full game restart. New in lua-bridge v0.3.0.
SaveVar.gotcha: A FLAT namespace shared by every mod on the machine, with no per-script isolation -- prefix every key with your script's own name or you'll collide with another mod's data. Numbers, strings and booleans only.

WsSend.doc: Broadcasts a line to every connected WebSocket client as {type:"ws", line:"..."}. Only exists in the WS-capable bridge build -- which is the one this IDE requires, and the channel every Run result comes back over.

Add.doc: Creates a marker offset from a target object: Marker.Add(nOffsetX, nOffsetY, nOffsetZ, uGuid, nR, nG, nB, nRadius). Confirmed in real scripts (e.g. mrxtaskobjectivedeliver.lua) — offset vector, target uGuid, RGB color, then a radius-looking value. Returns a marker handle later passed to Marker.Remove.

Add3D.doc: Attaches a 3D icon marker to an object: Marker.Add3D(uGuid, sIconName, nR, nG, nB [, nWidth]). Confirmed in real scripts (mrxtaskrace.lua) with icon names like "global_tripwirefinish" and "global_airring"; the optional trailing width was only seen paired with "global_airring". Returns a marker handle.

AddBlip.doc: Adds a minimap/radar blip to a uGuid: Marker.AddBlip(uGuid, sTextureName, nSize, nR, nG, nB, nAlpha, ...). The one function on this namespace confirmed by live in-game testing (see wiki snippets page); real scripts (mrxfactionmanager.lua) pass a longer arg list with nil gaps after texture/size/RGBA, so the full trailing parameter set beyond those is not individually confirmed.
AddBlip.gotcha: Renders at GROUND LEVEL under the object, not at the object's own height -- a known quirk of the one live-confirmed call. An untested texture name silently fails to load rather than erroring, so reuse a confirmed one instead of guessing.

AddDisc.doc: Draws a flat colored ring/disc on the ground: Marker.AddDisc(uGuidOrLocation, nRadius, nR, nG, nB, nThickness). Confirmed in real scripts; the first argument accepts either a uGuid or a raw location vector (e.g. mrxtaskobjectivedeliver.lua passes a vDestLoc vector directly instead of a uGuid).

AddTripwire.example: Marker.AddTripwire(x0, y0, z0, fWidth, yaw0, r, g, b)
AddTripwire.doc: Creates a tripwire marker at raw world coordinates: Marker.AddTripwire(nX, nY, nZ, nWidth, nYaw, nR, nG, nB). Confirmed in mrxtaskrace.lua, used for race-gate finish lines and typically paired with Add3D for the visual finish-line icon at the same location.

HaltPulse.doc: Marker.HaltPulse(uGuid) — stops a previously-started Marker.Pulse effect on the given object's marker. Confirmed in mrxfactionmanager.lua, called when tearing down a reporting-display marker.

Pulse.doc: Marker.Pulse(uGuid, nR, nG, nB) — flashes/pulses an object's existing marker in the given RGB color. Confirmed in real scripts (mrxfactionmanager.lua, munitions.lua); paired with HaltPulse to stop the effect. Takes a uGuid, not a marker handle.

Remove.doc: Marker.Remove(uMarker) — removes/cleans up a marker. Extremely common in real scripts; always called with the marker handle previously returned by Add, Add3D, AddBlip, AddDisc, or AddTripwire — not a raw object uGuid.
Remove.gotcha: The only thing that accepts a Marker.Add*() handle -- there is no clear-all native for markers, so a handle you lose track of leaks for the session. Register it with a tracker at creation time.

SetColor.doc: Recolours an existing marker. No call sites in the corpus -- the RGB signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Marker.Add*/Pulse functions.

SetFollowGuid.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The name suggests re-attaching an existing marker to follow a different object.

SetGroupedBlipLimit.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumably caps how many blips of a group collapse into a single minimap icon; corresponds by function, not exact name, to Gui._MarkerSetBlipLimit.

SetLocation.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The name suggests moving an existing marker to new world coordinates.

GetXZHeading.example: Math.GetXZHeading(tX - pX, tY - pY, tZ - pZ)

PolarToRect.doc: Named as a member of this table by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed a polar-to-rectangular coordinate conversion by name, but the argument shape is a guess, not a confirmed signature.

randf.gotcha: The ENGINE's own RNG, entirely independent of lua-bridge's polyfilled math.random -- two separate generators side by side, so seeding one has no effect on the other. Pick whichever matches the code you're extending and don't mix them.

CrossProduct.doc: Returns the 3-component cross product of two 3D vectors. Live-probed directly against a running game and the only member of this table with a fully live-confirmed argument and return shape.
CrossProduct.sig: cx, cy, cz = Math.CrossProduct(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz)

abs.doc: Named as an existing member of this table by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed absolute value by name; signature unconfirmed.

deg.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number. Read as radians-to-degrees from the name and from plausible degree-range values in the probe, but the exact conversion was not verified against reference values.
deg.gotcha: Capitalised Math is a native engine table, entirely unrelated to the lowercase Lua math table -- Math.deg and math.deg are not the same function.

exp.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number. Presumed the standard exponential function by name; not independently verified against known values.

round.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number.
round.gotcha: Rounding behaviour (half-up vs half-to-even, and whether a decimal-places argument is accepted) was never tested beyond the plain single-argument call.

AddMessage.doc: Queues an objective-style HUD message and returns a message-id table. Widely confirmed (resident/mrxguiinterface.lua's DisplayObjectiveMessage, resident/mrxsupport.lua, resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, several vz/ scripts); a minimal {sMessage = "..."} table works too.
AddMessage.sig: tMsgIds = Hud.MessageBox:AddMessage({sMessage=s, nPriority=n, nDuration=n, bClearBuffer=b, bAllowsAppends=b, fCallback=fn})
AddMessage.gotcha: Capture the returned id table -- it is what Hud.MessageBox:ModifyPendingMessage and RemovePendingMessage expect.

ModifyPendingMessage.doc: Rewrites a still-pending message in place, using the id table AddMessage returned, and returns a success boolean. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

RemovePendingMessage.doc: Removes a still-pending message. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take the same message-id table AddMessage returns, by analogy with ModifyPendingMessage.

SetGradient.doc: Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient(n1..n10) takes 10 numeric arguments and is confirmed called twice back-to-back at boot (e.g. (0,128,0,0,0,0,0,0.65,0.35,0) then (128,255,0,0.65,0.35,0,1,1,1,0)), presumably defining a two-stop shadow/highlight color-grading curve. Exact per-argument meaning is not confirmed.

AutoClient.doc: Returns whether the game should automatically connect as a client at boot. Used as `if Net.AutoClient() then Net.ConnectToServer() end` in gamebootstrap.lua and shellbootstrap.lua.

AutoLobby.doc: Returns whether the game should automatically enter the lobby at boot, the same boot-time chain as AutoClient/AutoServer: `elseif Net.AutoLobby() then Net.EnterLobby() end`.

AutoServer.doc: Returns whether the game should automatically start as a server at boot, part of the same boot-time branch as AutoClient: `if Net.AutoServer() then Net.StartServer(...) end`.

BeginLayerEventGroup.doc: Begins a bracketed group of layer-related network events. Called with no arguments and guarded by an existence check (`if Net.BeginLayerEventGroup then ... end`), confirmed in xQ!L.lua; paired with EndLayerEventGroup.

ConnectToServer.doc: Connects to a server, optionally with a name and an IP-address-or-mode string (e.g. "online" or an empty string for LAN); called with no arguments at boot to use defaults. Returns a boolean treated as success.

DoneReloadingLayers.doc: Signals that layer reloading has completed. Called with no arguments and consistently guarded by an existence check (`if Net.DoneReloadingLayers then ... end`) across several vz mission scripts and mrxtaskcontract.lua — the recurring guard suggests it may not exist on every engine build.

EndLayerEventGroup.doc: Ends a bracketed group of layer-related network events. Called with no arguments and guarded by an existence check, confirmed in xQ!L.lua; paired with BeginLayerEventGroup.

EnterFriendsLobby.doc: Enters the friends lobby. Called with no arguments in mrxguishell.lua.

EnterLobby.doc: Enters the multiplayer lobby. Called with no arguments at boot time and from shell-menu lobby entry.

ExitFriendsLobby.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Net) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Net.EnterFriendsLobby.

GetHostName.doc: Returns the local host's display name. Always used as the first argument to Net.StartServer(Net.GetHostName(), ...).
GetHostName.gotcha: The string this returns does NOT survive Net.SendCustomEvent -- it arrives on the other machine as an opaque lightuserdata handle, not the original text. Send a number the receiver can map back itself.

GrantAchievement.doc: Grants the named achievement (sAchievementName) locally on the machine that should actually be credited. Typically paired with a separate Net.SendCustomEvent call to notify the other side of the grant — that companion call does not grant it remotely, only informs.

HasPlayerUnlockedCode.doc: Returns whether the player has unlocked a particular code. Used with no arguments, e.g. to gate an outfit-unlock check: `if Net.HasPlayerUnlockedCode() and nCurrentOutfit ~= 2 then` in wifpmcinterior.lua.

IsActive.doc: Returns whether networking/an active session is currently running. Appears to be a distinct check from IsMultiplayer/IsServer, used as a general session-active gate in several resident and vz mission scripts.

IsClient.doc: Returns whether the local machine is a network client. Used both as `if Net.IsClient() then` and negated (`if not Net.IsClient() then`) to branch client-only vs. host/local-only logic.
IsClient.gotcha: Can read TRUE in single-player -- gating host-only logic on this alone silently no-ops everything for a solo player. Gate on `Net.IsMultiplayer() and Net.IsClient()` instead.

IsConnectedToInternet.doc: Returns whether the platform currently has an internet connection. Called with no arguments, e.g. in mrxguipda.lua.

IsMatchmakingInternet.doc: Returns whether matchmaking is set to internet mode versus local/LAN. Used throughout mrxguishell.lua's lobby-entry flow to branch internet vs. local matchmaking.

IsMultiplayer.doc: Returns whether the current session is multiplayer. Used standalone (e.g. `if not Net.IsMultiplayer() then`) and combined with IsServer, as in `(not Net.IsMultiplayer() or Net.IsServer())`.

IsOnlineConnected.doc: Returns whether the game is currently connected online. Used together with IsMatchmakingInternet to decide whether to call Net.Stop(), e.g. `if not Net.IsMatchmakingInternet() and not Net.IsOnlineConnected() then Net.Stop() end`.

IsPlatformConnected.doc: Returns whether the platform (e.g. Live/PSN) is connected. Combined with IsMatchmakingInternet in mrxguishell.lua to gate whether StartServer should be called.

IsReadyToTether.doc: Returns whether the client is ready to tether. Seen guarding tether logic alongside a vehicle-guid check: `if Net.IsReadyToTether() and not uCurrentVehicleGuid then` in meccon001.lua.

IsServer.doc: Returns whether the local machine is acting as the network server/host. It is the standard gate used before broadcasting a SendEvent_* call or mutating authoritative state, e.g. `if Net.IsServer() then Net.SendEvent_Fanfare(...) end`.

LoadMissionSpiel.doc: Loads mission briefing dialogue/actor data: `Net.LoadMissionSpiel(nMissionIndex, tNetBriefingActors)`, confirmed in mrxbriefing.lua.

QuitGame.doc: Quits the current game/session. Called with no arguments from the pause-menu quit option (mrxguipausescreen.lua) and from the end-of-game/credits flow (wifmissionflow.lua).

SendCustomEvent.doc: General-purpose broadcast for arbitrary mission-defined state: `Net.SendCustomEvent(sModuleName, iEventId, tArgs [, bReliable])`. sModuleName is a routing-key string matching the calling module's name, iEventId is a module-local numeric event ID, tArgs is an args table (often empty), and the optional trailing boolean requests reliable delivery. Unlike SendEvent_*, it is not consistently gated behind Net.IsServer() — some call sites fire it from either side.
SendCustomEvent.gotcha: Two live-confirmed payload traps: the event ID is MASKED to a small range (nEventId=100 arrived as 4, i.e. 100 mod 8) so keep custom IDs below 8, and STRING arguments do not survive as text -- they arrive as an opaque lightuserdata handle with no reverse lookup. Encode any arbitrary text as numbers; guids and counts cross intact.

SendEvent_AddDangerousBuilding.doc: Part of the Net.SendEvent_* family: a one-way, server-to-client broadcast of one specific named network event, used to keep HUD/UI/world state (fanfare cards, PDA and radar blips, objective markers, messages) identical on every client. Confirmed at resident/dangerousbuilding.lua:134. The wiki groups it with the family rather than giving it its own row, because its argument shape adds nothing beyond the family convention -- arguments match the data being synced.
SendEvent_AddDangerousBuilding.gotcha: Gate it behind Net.IsServer() -- every call site in the corpus does, sometimes with an extra condition such as not Player.IsLocal(uPlayerGuid).

AddLabel.doc: Adds a string label (sLabel) to uGuid, e.g. `Object.AddLabel(uHeli, "Disposable")`.

AddQualityRef.doc: Registers a quality reference (nQuality) on uGuid and returns a reference handle that call sites store and later pass to RemoveQualityRef.
AddQualityRef.gotcha: One of the engine's leak-prone Add.../Remove... pairs: the handle it returns is only accepted by its own matching Remove call, and there is NO "clear everything I made" native for it. Track every handle yourself or it leaks for the session.

AddToDisposer.doc: Registers uGuid with the disposer/cleanup system under a category string (sCategory), e.g. "Vehicle".
AddToDisposer.gotcha: Leak-prone Add/Remove pair -- only RemoveFromDisposer undoes it and there is no clear-all native. Register the handle with a tracker at creation time, not at teardown time.

ApplyImpulse.doc: Applies a physics impulse to uGuid along (nX, nY, nZ) plus a trailing boolean flag, e.g. `Object.ApplyImpulse(uGuid, 0, 10000, 6 * myMass, true)`.
ApplyImpulse.gotcha: Confirmed to do NOTHING to a standing player character (works on vehicles and physics props only). In local space the axes are (x=side, y=up, z=forward), and a real boost scales the impulse by Object.GetMass -- impulse is mass*dV, so an unscaled value shoves a bike and barely nudges a tank.

ApplyPointImpulse.doc: Applies an impulse to uGuid using 6 numeric components plus a trailing boolean, e.g. `Object.ApplyPointImpulse(uGuid, 0, 10*myMass, 0.1*myMass, 0, 0, 0.15, true)`. Call-site patterns suggest an impulse vector plus an application-point offset, but the exact meaning of each component isn't confirmed.
ApplyPointImpulse.gotcha: Applying the impulse at an OFF-CENTER point imparts spin (torque), not just a push -- that's how the barrel-roll flip works, and why an accidental non-zero offset makes things tumble. Same no-effect-on-a-standing-player limit as Object.ApplyImpulse.

Attach.doc: Attaches uChildGuid to uParentGuid at a named hardpoint (sHardpoint). Returns a success boolean and, per at least one call site, an attachment handle for the newly attached instance.

AttachCargoToWinch.doc: Attaches uCargo to the winch of uHeli — cargo object first, then the winching vehicle.

CloseGate.doc: Closes a gate object; always paired with OpenGate in the same modules.

Detach.doc: Detaches uChildOrAttachmentGuid from uParentGuid, returning a success boolean.

DetachCargoFromWinch.doc: Detaches whatever cargo is on the winch of uHeli, taking only the winching vehicle's uGuid.

DisablePhysics.doc: Disables physics simulation on uGuid. Very common in real scripts, and always paired with EnablePhysics elsewhere in the same modules.

EnablePhysics.doc: Re-enables physics simulation on uGuid. Always found paired with DisablePhysics in the same modules.

FadeOut.doc: Fades out uGuid over nDuration seconds, plus a trailing boolean flag, e.g. `Object.FadeOut(uVehicle, 0.2, true)`.

GetAttachedObjects.doc: Returns a table/list of objects attached to uGuid, e.g. `tSeats = Object.GetAttachedObjects(uTruck)` to enumerate a vehicle's seats.

GetCashValue.doc: Returns the object's cash value, e.g. used to compute a collectible's cash reward.

GetDistanceFrom.doc: Returns the distance from uGuidA to either another object (uGuidB) or explicit coordinates (nX, nY, nZ), with an optional bIgnoreY flag to ignore vertical distance. Both call forms are confirmed in real scripts.

GetHardpointPosition.doc: Returns the x, y, z world position of a named hardpoint (sHardpointName) on the object, e.g. `Object.GetHardpointPosition(uMainTruck, "HP_Truckbed")`.
GetHardpointPosition.gotcha: A freshly Pg.Spawn'd model's hardpoints return nil for roughly 0.3s while the skeleton initializes -- reading them synchronously at spawn time silently fails and looks like "the bone name is wrong". Poll until it first returns non-nil (the player character is always ready; a just-spawned vehicle is not).

GetHealth.doc: Returns the object's current numeric health value. Extremely common in real scripts, always called with a plain uGuid.

GetHibernationDistance.doc: Returns the distance at which uGuid hibernates/streams out, e.g. compared against an AI's aggro range.

GetLocalizedName.doc: Returns the localized/display name of uGuid; very common for HUD/display text. One call site passes an extra boolean argument whose meaning is unconfirmed.

GetMass.doc: Returns the object's mass as a numeric value, e.g. `local myMass = Object.GetMass(uGuid)`.

GetMaxHealth.doc: Returns the object's maximum health value; commonly paired with GetHealth for HUD/health-bar display.

GetName.doc: Returns the object's internal/debug name — contrast with the player-facing GetLocalizedName.
GetName.gotcha: Sometimes returns a bare USERDATA instead of a string or nil -- a confirmed live finding, not hypothetical -- and can throw outright for some objects. Type-check the result before concatenating it, and pcall the call itself.

GetNodeHealth.doc: Returns the health of a specific destructible sub-part/node on the object, identified by sNodeName.

GetParent.doc: Returns the parent object of uGuid; commonly used to walk up an attachment/ownership chain.

GetPosition.doc: Returns the x, y, z world position of the object identified by uGuid. Confirmed working via live testing and widely used in real scripts, e.g. combined with Player.GetLocalCharacter().
GetPosition.gotcha: Returns THREE separate values (x, y, z), not a table -- and capturing fewer (`local x, y = Object.GetPosition(...)`) silently drops the rest rather than erroring.

GetVelocity.doc: Returns the object's current speed. Call sites treat the return value as a single scalar, not a vector.

GetYaw.doc: Returns the object's yaw as a single number. The unit (degrees vs. radians) is unconfirmed — sample scripts disagree, one implying degrees and another implying radians via a hand-tuned correction factor, so don't trust either assumption without testing.
GetYaw.gotcha: On a character this is the CHEST/BODY orientation, not where the player is LOOKING -- swing the mouse and the view rotates while this value does not, so "spawn in front of me" lands in front of the body. The unit (degrees vs radians) is also unconfirmed; the wiki's own sample scripts disagree, so test rather than assume.

HasLabel.doc: Returns whether uGuid has the given string label. Extremely common in real scripts, e.g. `Object.HasLabel(uGuid, "PMC")`.

InSeat.doc: Returns the vehicle uGuid the object is seated in, if any; the return value is treated as a vehicle handle at call sites.

InVehicle.doc: Returns the vehicle uGuid the object is currently inside, if any, e.g. `local uVeh = Object.InVehicle(uRunner)`.

InsideBoundary.doc: Returns whether uGuid is inside the zone/region object uZoneGuid, with an optional bIgnoreY flag, e.g. testing a character against a named warehouse region.

IsAlive.doc: Returns whether uGuid is alive. Extremely common check in real scripts, always a plain uGuid argument.

IsAttached.doc: Returns whether two objects (uGuidA, uGuidB) are attached to each other, e.g. checking a player against a designator object.

IsAwake.doc: Returns whether uGuid is currently awake (not hibernated/streamed out); related to the hibernation-distance system alongside GetHibernationDistance.

IsDisguised.doc: Returns whether the character uGuid is currently disguised.

IsHibernated.doc: Returns whether uGuid is currently hibernated, e.g. `if Object.IsHibernated(self.exec.guid) then`.

IsPlayerControlled.doc: Returns whether uGuid is currently player-driven rather than AI-driven. Very common, used to distinguish AI vs. player-controlled vehicles/characters.

IsTemplate.doc: Returns whether uGuid is a template object rather than a live instance.

IsValid.doc: Returns whether uGuid still refers to a valid, existing object, e.g. `if Object.IsValid(civAmbulance) then`.

IsVisible.doc: Returns whether uGuid is currently visible.
IsVisible.gotcha: Engine getters return 1/0, not true/false -- and 0 is TRUTHY in Lua, so `not Object.IsVisible(g)` never flips. Compare explicitly (`== 1`) or track a real boolean in _G instead.

IsWinched.doc: Returns whether uGuid is currently attached/winched, e.g. `if Object.IsWinched(uGuid) then`.

Kill.doc: Kills the object identified by uGuid. Presumed destructive/irreversible like other teardown calls in this codebase, though that hasn't been separately verified via live testing.

OpenGate.doc: Opens a gate object such as a garage, e.g. `Object.OpenGate(self.garage)`.

OutsideBoundary.doc: Returns whether uGuid is outside the zone/region object uZoneGuid, e.g. checking a vehicle against its containing region.

PlayAnimation.doc: Plays animation sAnimName on uGuid with a loop flag, channel name (sChannel, can be nil), blend time, and a trailing boolean flag. Confirmed with all 6 arguments in real scripts, e.g. hijack animations.

PlayMaterialAnimation.doc: Plays a material animation sAnimName on uGuid with a loop flag, e.g. `Object.PlayMaterialAnimation(uGuid, "global_gpsjammer_anim", true)`.

Remove.doc: Removes/destroys the object identified by uGuid. Extremely common; presumed irreversible like Kill, though not separately verified via live testing.

RemoveLabel.doc: Removes a string label (sLabel) from uGuid, e.g. `Object.RemoveLabel(uVehicle, "garage")`.

RemoveQualityRef.doc: Releases a quality reference previously obtained from AddQualityRef; takes that returned ref value, not a raw uGuid.

Revive.doc: Revives uGuid, with an optional numeric second argument that call-site patterns suggest is a delay, e.g. `Object.Revive(uChar, 0.5)`.

SetHealth.doc: Sets the object's health to nHealth, e.g. `Object.SetHealth(uJeep, 8)`. Also used to fully heal via `Object.SetHealth(uGuid, Object.GetMaxHealth(uGuid))`.

SetHibernationDistance.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed to pair with the confirmed Object.GetHibernationDistance / Object.RevertHibernationDistance.

SetInfiniteAmmo.doc: Toggles infinite ammo on uGuid. Confirmed working via live testing — note it maxes out reserve ammo, not the currently loaded magazine.

SetInvincible.doc: Toggles invincibility on uGuid. The optional 3rd argument is a string "reason" tag consistently used to name the source of invincibility, e.g. "Survival", "Hijack", "HQ", "Fanfare".

SetModelName.doc: Sets the model name (sModelName) used for uGuid.

SetName.doc: Sets the object's name to sName and returns a success boolean, e.g. `local bSuccess = Object.SetName(Mendez_Spawn, "Mendez")`.

SetPosition.doc: Sets the object's position to (x, y, z). Real scripts sometimes pass an optional 4th boolean-looking argument (e.g. `false`) whose meaning is unconfirmed.
SetPosition.gotcha: Silently no-ops on a spawned AI HUMAN -- same call, same coordinates that smoothly move a prop or vehicle just leave the soldier where it spawned (workaround: re-spawn the ghost each tick). It also doesn't visually propagate under a plain world-pause until Player.SetCinematicMode is also active.

SetTransformToObject.doc: Snaps uGuid's transform to match uTargetGuid, optionally at a named hardpoint (sHardpoint) on the target. Confirmed used both with just two uGuids and with an explicit hardpoint-name string argument.

SetUnkillable.doc: Toggles unkillable state on uGuid, using the same (bFlag, sReason) shape as SetInvincible, e.g. reason "Support".

SetVisible.doc: Sets the visibility of uGuid to bVisible.

SetWinchState.doc: Sets the winch state of uGuid to a string state; the only confirmed value seen in real scripts is "deployed".

SetYaw.doc: Sets the object's yaw to nYaw. Same degrees-vs-radians unit ambiguity noted for GetYaw applies here too.
SetYaw.gotcha: Unit and axis convention is UNCONFIRMED -- one wiki sample treats the value as degrees, another applies an empirically fudged radian correction. Test before trusting either.

StopAllAnimation.doc: Stops all animation playback on uGuid.

StopAnimationChannel.doc: Stops animation playback on a specific named channel (sChannel) of uGuid, matching the channel argument used in PlayAnimation, e.g. `Object.StopAnimationChannel(self._vehicle, "hijack")`.

StopMaterialAnimation.doc: Stops a named material animation (sAnimName) on uGuid, e.g. `Object.StopMaterialAnimation(uGuid, "global_weapon_beacon")`.

ApplyAngularImpulse.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; arguments beyond the presumed leading uGuid are unconfirmed.

AreEqual.doc: Compares two object guids and returns a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the decompiled corpus.

BeginQueuedAcceleration.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumably pairs with Object.QueueAcceleration, but that pairing is inferred from naming only.

GetHardpointPitch.doc: Returns a named hardpoint's pitch in degrees. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, settling an earlier by-analogy guess; still no call sites in the corpus.

GetHardpointYaw.doc: Returns a named hardpoint's yaw in degrees. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, settling an earlier by-analogy guess; still no call sites in the corpus.

GetHeightAboveTerrain.doc: Returns an object's height above ground or seabed, in metres. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- useful for altitude checks on aircraft or dropped cargo.
GetHeightAboveTerrain.gotcha: The return meaning comes from the live probe, not from source: there are no call sites anywhere in the corpus.

GetInvincible.doc: Returns whether an object is currently invincible, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the corpus.

GetModelName.doc: Returns an object's model name-hash handle. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
GetModelName.gotcha: Returns userdata, NOT a string, despite the name. String concatenation and string.* calls will not work on the result without conversion -- treat it as an opaque handle.

GetVelocitySquared.doc: Returns speed squared -- the squared magnitude of the object's velocity. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; handy for distance/speed comparisons without a square root.
GetVelocitySquared.gotcha: Squared, not raw speed: compare against a squared threshold, or take the square root before treating it as a speed.

GetVelocityVector.doc: Returns the object's velocity as three components, vx, vy, vz. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
GetVelocityVector.gotcha: Returns three values where the similarly-named Object.GetVelocity returns a single scalar.

GetWinchState.doc: Reads a winch's state. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 only on a non-winch object, where it returns nil.
GetWinchState.gotcha: nil on a non-winch object is expected behaviour, not a bug. What it returns on an object that does have a winch was never exercised -- the setter uses string states like "deployed", so a string return is inferred, not confirmed.

HasWinch.doc: Returns whether an object has a winch, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- the safe guard to call before the rest of the winch family.

IsWinching.doc: Reports whether a winch is currently winching. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 only on a non-winch object, where it returns nil.
IsWinching.gotcha: nil on a non-winch object is expected behaviour, not evidence of a broken call -- gate on Object.HasWinch first.

RemoveFromDisposer.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Object.AddToDisposer.

SetPositionToObject.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus.
SetPositionToObject.gotcha: The signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Object.SetTransformToObject -- treat with caution.

TransformLocalToWorld.doc: Converts a point from an object's local space to world space, returning x, y, z. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- reach for it to place something at an offset from a moving or rotated object.
TransformLocalToWorld.sig: x, y, z = Object.TransformLocalToWorld(uGuid, lx, ly, lz)
TransformLocalToWorld.gotcha: The signature comes from the live probe, not source: there are no call sites anywhere in the corpus.

AddObject.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to add a specific object guid into a filter's candidate set; signature unconfirmed.

Create.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to construct a new filter handle -- the first step of an inferred Create/AddObject/SetFilter/SetRelation/Eval builder pattern.
Create.gotcha: The builder-pattern reading of this namespace is inference from names alone; no signature is confirmed for any member.

Eval.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to evaluate a configured filter and return its matches; signature unconfirmed.

GetCoopPlayerGuid.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed.
GetCoopPlayerGuid.gotcha: Does not obviously fit the Create/AddObject/SetFilter/SetRelation/Eval builder reading -- plausibly a convenience getter feeding a co-op player's guid into a filter, but its relationship to the other five is not confirmed.

SetFilter.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to set a filter predicate on a filter handle; signature unconfirmed.

SetRelation.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to set a relational condition (combining criteria, or a spatial/faction relation) on a filter handle; signature unconfirmed.

StartEmitter.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to start a particle emitter attached to an object, but the argument shape is a guess from the name only.

SendMessage.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by naming to send a message/signal to an object.
SendMessage.gotcha: A leading-uGuid argument shape is a guess by analogy with other namespaces, not a confirmed signature.

ClearSlot.doc: Clears one numbered objective-tray slot. Extremely common in vz/ mission scripts, both as ClearSlot({vPlayer = nil, nSlot = 1}) and the shorter ClearSlot({nSlot = 1}).
ClearSlot.gotcha: The vPlayer field appears to be optional -- both forms occur in shipped scripts.

SetSlotToImage.doc: Puts an image in an objective-tray slot. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua alongside SetSlotToText in the same dispatch function; the exact field list was not fully confirmed.

SetSlotToText.doc: Sets the text shown in one of the small numbered objective-tray slots. Dozens of confirmed call sites across vz/ mission scripts -- the standard way to drive on-screen objective text.

SetSlotToWidget.doc: Puts a widget in an objective-tray slot. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed similar in shape to SetSlotToText/SetSlotToImage.

AchievementAddCount.doc: Increments progress toward an achievement: AchievementAddCount(sAchievementName, nIndex, nDelta, nRequiredCount).

AchievementIsGranted.doc: Checks whether an achievement has been granted: AchievementIsGranted(sAchievementName, nIndex, nRequiredCount); returns a boolean.

AddContextAction.doc: Adds a context/interaction action prompt to an object: AddContextAction(uGuid, sLabelOrKey, nPriority?, ...). Only the guid and label/localization-key are confirmed as a fixed schema; trailing args vary widely (0 to 6 extra values) across call sites, likely priority/range/color/flags, and the call often returns a success boolean.
AddContextAction.gotcha: Leak-prone Add/Remove pair with no clear-all native -- only RemoveContextAction accepts the handle. Track it at creation or it survives for the session.

AssetExists.doc: Checks whether a named asset/layer of a given type exists: AssetExists(sLayerName, sType).

ClearCustomPursuit.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed the inverse of Pg.SetCustomPursuit by naming, unconfirmed.

ClearPursuitLock.doc: Clears a pursuit lock: ClearPursuitLock(bFlag). Confirmed to take a single boolean argument; also seen passed as a bare function reference elsewhere.

ContractActivated.doc: Marks a mission contract as activated: ContractActivated(sMissionName).

ContractCancelled.doc: Marks the current mission contract as cancelled; called with no arguments.

ContractCompleted.doc: Marks the current mission contract as completed; called with no arguments.

EnableIntersection.doc: Enables or disables a road intersection: EnableIntersection(bEnable, uGuid).

FastCollectBuildings.doc: Collects nearby buildings within a radius: FastCollectBuildings(x, y, z, fRadius, sFilter?), e.g. filtering by "Occupied". Filter argument is confirmed optional by call sites both with and without it.

FastCollectFlying.doc: Collects nearby flying objects within a radius: FastCollectFlying(x, y, z, fRadius). The one call site found passes no filter argument.

FastCollectGroundVehicles.doc: Collects nearby ground vehicles within a radius: FastCollectGroundVehicles(x, y, z, fRadius, sFilter?). The filter is confirmed optional (callable with or without it) and not strictly a string — one call site passes a filter object (oFilter) instead of a plain string.

FastCollectHelicopters.doc: Collects nearby helicopters within a radius: FastCollectHelicopters(x, y, z, fRadius). No filter argument observed in its call site.

FastCollectHumans.doc: Collects nearby human/character objects within a radius: FastCollectHumans(x, y, z, fRadius, sFilter?). Filter is a string, sometimes a compound expression like "Allied && Human" or "OC && Human"; every observed call site for this function includes the filter.
FastCollectHumans.gotcha: Has no concept of "self": a radius query centered on the player returns the player's own character(s) exactly like any other nearby human, indistinguishably. A confirmed real incident had a sweep return only the player's own guid and a destructive call on the result killed the player -- filter yourself out explicitly.

FastCollectTanks.doc: Collects nearby tanks within a radius: FastCollectTanks(x, y, z, fRadius). The one call site found passes no filter argument.

FindPointFromCamera.doc: Computes a world point relative to the current camera: FindPointFromCamera(nForwardOffset, nHeightOrAltitude, nUnknown, uOwner?, nAngle?); returns x, y, z. Very widely used; the third positional argument is consistently -1 or a small number across sites but its exact meaning isn't confirmed beyond that.

GetDistantSpawnPointOnPath.doc: Finds a spawn point along a path relative to primary/secondary reference points and a minimum distance: GetDistantSpawnPointOnPath(uPath, uBackupPointOrPrimaryPt, nSecondaryPt, fDist); returns a result flag plus x, y, z, yaw.

GetGuidByName.doc: Resolves a level-designer-assigned name string to a GUID: GetGuidByName(sName), e.g. Pg.GetGuidByName("China"). Extremely widely used; also reachable as a bare unqualified global GetGuidByName(...) in many scripts, apparently aliased onto _G in addition to living on Pg (same name used interchangeably in adjacent statements in vz/allcon001.lua).
GetGuidByName.gotcha: Returns only ONE guid even when many objects in the world match that name. It also genuinely has nothing to find for anything in a region that hasn't streamed yet -- e.g. an outpost building queried from an OnLoad script while the session starts inside the PMC HQ interior.

GetLineRegionPoints.doc: Gets the point arrays defining a line region: GetLineRegionPoints(uRegionGuid, bInvert?); returns two tables (tX, tY) of coordinates.

GetLoadingStaticLayers.doc: Getter counterpart of LoadingStaticLayers; returns the current loading-static-layers flag with no arguments.

GetObjectsInArea.doc: Finds objects in a radius matching a named filter/template type: GetObjectsInArea(x, y, z, fRadius, sFilterName), e.g. "Listening Post", "RumJug", "Vehicle". Unlike the FastCollect* family, the filter argument appears mandatory in every observed call site.

GetPursuitState.doc: Returns the current pursuit-state value/table; called with no arguments.

GetUnloadingStaticLayers.doc: Getter counterpart of UnloadingStaticLayers; returns the current unloading-static-layers flag with no arguments.

IsPointInBoundary.doc: Checks whether a world point lies within a named boundary object: IsPointInBoundary(x, y, z, uBoundaryGuid).

IsStaticLayer.doc: Checks whether a named layer is a static layer: IsStaticLayer(sLayerName); used to guard both add and remove layer requests.

LoadAsset.doc: Loads a named asset of a given type: LoadAsset(sAssetName, sAssetType, ...), e.g. animations or sound banks. A third argument (like a sound duck-table) is sometimes present and sometimes omitted.

LoadLayer.doc: Loads a static/streaming layer by name: LoadLayer(sLayerName, bNotStatic, fCallback, tCallbackData, bClientNeedsLoadingScreen); returns a success boolean.
LoadLayer.gotcha: Calling this directly bypasses MrxLayerManager's _tLoadedLayers bookkeeping -- the single source of truth the native save reads -- leaving the save's idea of the world desynced from the actual world. Route layer changes through MrxLayerManager instead.

LoadingStaticLayers.doc: Setter that flags whether static layers are currently loading: LoadingStaticLayers(bFlag). Distinct from the getter GetLoadingStaticLayers despite the similar name.

LockPursuit.doc: Locks pursuit at a given level for a guid: LockPursuit(uGuid, nLevel).

ReloadLayer.doc: Reloads a layer by name: ReloadLayer(sLayerName, fCallback, tCallbackData, bClientNeedsLoadingScreen).

RemoveContextAction.doc: Removes a context action from an object: RemoveContextAction(uGuid); consistently called with just the guid, mirroring AddContextAction.

ResetSingletonDone.doc: Resets a singleton-done flag/state; called with no arguments.

Rumble.doc: Triggers controller rumble for a character: Rumble(uCharacterGuid, fLength).

SaveGame.gotcha: Two independent pieces of code stashing-and-swapping this function will silently clobber each other -- a confirmed interleaving had one system's restore discard another's freshly installed wrap, leaving that system's save-gate permanently ineffective for the session. Install ONE wrap, never uninstall it, and gate by refcount.

SetBoundaryRadius.doc: Sets the boundary radius: SetBoundaryRadius(fRadius), e.g. Pg.SetBoundaryRadius(38.5).

SetCustomPursuit.doc: Sets a custom pursuit configuration for a faction: SetCustomPursuit(uFaction, nDuration, tSettings), where tSettings is a table of settings.

SetPursuit.doc: Sets the pursuit level for a faction: SetPursuit(uFaction, nLevel, bFlag).

SetPursuitLevelTimes.doc: Sets timing thresholds between pursuit levels: SetPursuitLevelTimes(nTime1, nTime2), e.g. Pg.SetPursuitLevelTimes(120, 300).

SetPursuitSeconds.doc: Sets a pursuit duration in seconds for a faction: SetPursuitSeconds(uFaction, nSeconds, bFlag).

Spawn.doc: Spawns an object/vehicle/character by template name string at a world position: Spawn(sTemplateName, x, y, z, ...). Extensively confirmed elsewhere in the wiki with real template strings, e.g. supply drop templates called as Pg.Spawn(sTemplate, x, y+200, z).
Spawn.gotcha: A blank or unresolved template string CRASHES THE GAME TO DESKTOP -- this is a native crash, not a Lua error, so pcall cannot catch it (live-confirmed with Pg.Spawn('Austin (CIV)', ...)). Validate first: Pg.GetGuidByName(name) ~= nil, every time.

SpawnFromCamera.doc: Spawns an object relative to the current camera: SpawnFromCamera(sTemplateName, nDistance, nHeightOrScale, ...). Call-site argument counts vary from 3 to 7; trailing args include booleans and an owner/player guid, but their exact meaning beyond the first three positions is unconfirmed.

StartHeliWaveSpawner.example: Pg.StartHeliWaveSpawner({ tWave1, tWave2, tWave3, tWave4, tWave5, tWave6 })
StartHeliWaveSpawner.doc: Starts a helicopter wave spawner from a single parameter table: StartHeliWaveSpawner(tParams); the table's internal contents are not enumerated on this page.

StopHeliWaveSpawner.doc: Stops a helicopter wave spawner: StopHeliWaveSpawner(oSelf); also seen passed around as a bare function reference.

UnloadAsset.doc: Unloads a previously loaded asset: UnloadAsset(sAssetName, sAssetType); mirrors LoadAsset.

UnloadLayer.doc: Unloads a layer by name: UnloadLayer(sLayerName, fCallback, tCallbackData, bClientNeedsLoadingScreen).
UnloadLayer.gotcha: Same desync hazard as Pg.LoadLayer: unloading behind MrxLayerManager's back leaves _tLoadedLayers (what the native save reads) wrong. Also beware layer names that read like status flags -- 'pristine' turned out to be load-bearing geometry, and unloading it produced destroyed-and-empty bases.

UnloadingStaticLayers.doc: Setter that flags whether static layers are currently unloading: UnloadingStaticLayers(bFlag); mirrors LoadingStaticLayers.

AddSkirmishTemplate.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash, but no visible effect was observable from an isolated test spot and the exact argument shape was not pinned down.

AdjustPursuitLevel.doc: Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash. No visible effect from an isolated test spot -- it needs an actively engaged pursuit with faction units present to show what it adjusts.
AdjustPursuitLevel.gotcha: A live lead, not a settled signature: the exact argument shape was never pinned down.

AdjustPursuitTimer.doc: Live-probed 2026-07-22, same story as Pg.AdjustPursuitLevel: executes without error or crash, no visible effect observable in isolation, exact argument shape not pinned down.

ClearPursuitRestrictions.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; argument shape and actual restriction-clearing effect are unconfirmed.
ClearPursuitRestrictions.gotcha: Drops the organic-escalation restrictions only; it has no effect on a pursuit that is already running. Clearing restrictions is not the same as clearing heat.

FastCollectBoats.doc: Returns a table of boat guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, matching the rest of the FastCollect* family shape.
FastCollectBoats.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on FastCollectHumans/FastCollectGroundVehicles was not exercised for this member -- presumed present by family pattern, not confirmed.

FastCollectCars.doc: Returns a table of car guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 in the same probe as Pg.FastCollectBoats.
FastCollectCars.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

FastCollectGroundVehiclesExceptTanks.doc: Returns a table of ground-vehicle guids within fRadius of (x, y, z), excluding tanks -- the filtered sibling of Pg.FastCollectGroundVehicles. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
FastCollectGroundVehiclesExceptTanks.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

FastCollectJets.doc: Returns a table of jet guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
FastCollectJets.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

FastCollectProps.doc: Returns a table of prop guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
FastCollectProps.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

FastCollectUsables.doc: Returns a table of usable-object guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
FastCollectUsables.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

GetAllGuidsByName.doc: Returns a table of every guid matching a designer-assigned name, e.g. Pg.GetAllGuidsByName('L300') returned {800075FD}. Reach for it instead of Pg.GetGuidByName when several objects share one name. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
GetAllGuidsByName.gotcha: Returns a table, where the near-identically-named Pg.GetGuidByName returns a single guid. Zero call sites anywhere in the corpus -- the signature comes from the live probe, not from source.

GetBoundaryRadius.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
GetBoundaryRadius.gotcha: Despite the naming symmetry it is not confirmed as the getter for the global Pg.SetBoundaryRadius(fRadius) setter -- it takes a guid where that setter takes none, so it is more likely a per-object/per-boundary query. Treat the pairing as naming-only.

GetTetherDiameterEnd.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; its sibling Pg.GetTetherDiameterStart was not part of that probe batch and remains unconfirmed.

GetWarningRadius.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

ReloadAsset.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to combine unload and load by naming, unconfirmed.

RestrictAllPursuit.doc: Takes a boolean and blocks organic pursuit escalation -- the game's own AI-driven pursuit triggers. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; reach for it to keep the world calm during a scripted sequence.
RestrictAllPursuit.gotcha: Does NOT clear an active pursuit despite the name, and does not block a scripted pursuit start -- it only gates ORGANIC, AI-driven heat escalation. The off switch for a live chase is Pg.ClearPursuitLock(true), nothing else.

RestrictPursuitFaction.doc: Takes a faction guid and a boolean, blocking that one faction's organic pursuit escalation. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
RestrictPursuitFaction.gotcha: Gates only ORGANIC AI escalation for that faction -- it does not clear an already-active pursuit and does not block a scripted start. Use Pg.ClearPursuitLock(true) to actually end a chase.

SetGlobalSkirmishState.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director rather than asset streaming, despite where it originally appeared in the dump. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22: accepted both a boolean and an integer without erroring, but showed no visible effect from an isolated test spot -- it needs an actively engaged skirmish to observe.

SetMaxPursuitLevel.doc: Caps the pursuit level ceiling: after Pg.SetMaxPursuitLevel(2), a following Pg.SetPursuit(uFaction, 5) only reached Level=2. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
SetMaxPursuitLevel.gotcha: A ONE-WAY RATCHET DOWN for the rest of the session: nothing raises the ceiling back up. A bigger n, a (faction, n) form, 99, SetPursuitLevelTimes and SetCustomPursuit were all tried and none undo it -- only a save-load or full restart resets it.

SetSkirmishTable.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash, but no visible effect was observable from an isolated test spot and the exact argument shape was not pinned down.

SpawnPlayerAdvanced.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus and no confirmed usage. Explicitly flagged as still unmapped after the 2026-07-22 live-confirmation pass -- a known gap needing a dedicated probing pass.

SpawnRelative.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to spawn relative to an anchor object by naming symmetry with Pg.SpawnFromCamera, but that is inference, not evidence; still unmapped after the 2026-07-22 pass.

AddBoundary.doc: Registers a boundary zone (uBoundaryGuid) for a player (uPlayerGuid). Part of the mission/region boundary system where crossing fires a callback and can optionally be lethal.

AddCash.doc: Adds nAmount to the player's cash. Shares the same HUD-refresh-skipping nuance as SetCash.

AddFuel.doc: Adds nAmount to the player's fuel. No direct call sites; presumed counterpart to AddCash by naming symmetry, and likely (unconfirmed) shares the same HUD-refresh-skipping nuance as SetCash — prefer MrxPmc.AddFuelQty instead.

ClearGPS.doc: Clears GPS markers for a player, e.g. `Player.ClearGPS(Player.GetLocalPlayer())`.

ClearPlayerDB.doc: Clears the player database with no arguments, e.g. `Player.ClearPlayerDB()` in mrxplayer.lua.

GetAllCharacters.doc: Returns all character guids with no arguments; used as a target-filter value passed directly into proximity/collect calls.

GetAllPlayers.doc: Returns a table of all players with no arguments, e.g. `tPlayers = Player.GetAllPlayers()`.

GetAllTargetMarkerPos.doc: Returns a table of all target marker positions with no arguments, e.g. used in mrxguipda.lua.

GetAnyCharacter.doc: Returns a character guid used as a generic target-filter value (e.g. passed as `vTgtInclude`) in mission/objective scripts. Always called with no arguments.

GetAvailableCostumes.doc: Returns the count of costumes available to the player, no arguments. Distinct from the resident-module wrapper WifPmcInterior.GetAvailableCostumes(), which this engine function likely underlies (exact relationship unconfirmed).

GetCamera.doc: Given a player guid, returns that player's camera guid, e.g. `Player.GetCamera(uPlayer)`. The result is then passed into Camera.* calls.

GetCameraXZHeading.doc: Given a player guid, returns a heading/rotation value for that player's camera, used to rotate HUD compass elements, e.g. `Player.GetCameraXZHeading(oWidget:GetOwner())`.

GetCash.doc: Returns the player's current cash amount with no arguments. Confirmed working by live testing.

GetCharacter.doc: Given a player-slot guid, returns the corresponding character guid, e.g. `Player.GetCharacter(tData.uPlayerGuid)` — the character-guid counterpart to a raw player guid.

GetControlBindingType.doc: Given a player guid, returns a string describing that player's control scheme (used for pause-screen control-scheme display).

GetControlledObject.doc: Given a player guid, returns the guid of the character or vehicle that player currently controls. Extremely common in real scripts.

GetCurrentPlayers.doc: Returns a count with no arguments, treated in real scripts as a truthy multiplayer flag, e.g. `local isMultiplayer = Player.GetCurrentPlayers()`.

GetFuel.doc: Returns the player's current fuel with no arguments. Wrapped by MrxPmc.GetFuelQty(), confirmed by live testing to be a thin wrapper over this function.

GetFuelCapacity.doc: Returns the player's fuel capacity with no arguments. No direct call sites; presumed backing store for MrxPmc.GetFuelCapacity().

GetLocalCharacter.doc: Returns the local player's character guid with no arguments. Confirmed working by live testing and widely used in real scripts.

GetLocalPlayer.doc: Returns the local player-slot guid, distinct from the character guid. Takes no arguments; extremely common in real scripts.

GetPlayerStart.doc: Returns the player's spawn/start location with no arguments. Real code compares the result directly to a string constant, suggesting it can return a named-location string as well as a position (which form is canonical is unconfirmed).

GetPrimaryCharacter.doc: Returns the primary player's character guid with no arguments. Used throughout mods, e.g. for toggling infinite ammo or function-override examples.

GetPrimaryPlayer.doc: Returns the primary player's guid with no arguments, e.g. `Player.SetAimMode(Player.GetPrimaryPlayer(), true)`. Very common in real scripts.

GetProfileCostume.doc: Returns the player's currently selected costume index with no arguments.

GetSecondaryCharacter.doc: Returns the secondary (co-op) player's character guid with no arguments, used when a mod needs to also affect the second player.
GetSecondaryCharacter.gotcha: Correctly returns nil outside co-op -- pass that nil through rather than coercing it, or it reaches a downstream Object.* call expecting a real guid. This, not Player.GetSecondaryPlayer, is the reliable "are we in co-op" test.

GetSecondaryPlayer.doc: Returns the secondary (co-op) player's guid with no arguments. Call sites routinely guard it with `if Player.GetSecondaryPlayer() then` since it can be absent outside co-op.
GetSecondaryPlayer.gotcha: Returns a REAL, distinct, non-nil player-slot guid even in single-player (confirmed live) -- so `Player.GetSecondaryPlayer() ~= nil` is NOT a co-op check and will false-positive. Use Player.GetSecondaryCharacter(), which really does return nil outside co-op.

GetTargetUnderReticle.doc: Given a player guid, returns `nX, nY, nZ` world coordinates plus a 4th `uGuid` return value identifying whatever is under the player's reticle (nil if nothing targeted). Confirmed used in mrxguisatellite.lua and mrxguisniperscope.lua via `oWidget:GetOwner()`.
GetTargetUnderReticle.gotcha: Confirmed to exist, but its only two real call sites in the whole decompiled corpus are special targeting-overlay contexts (the satellite support-call screen and the sniper scope) -- its behaviour under the NORMAL player camera is unconfirmed. A low-radius Pg.FastCollect* sweep sorted by distance is the approach that was actually verified.

GetVehicleDisguise.doc: Returns whether vehicle disguise is currently active, no arguments; treated as a boolean state flag, e.g. for HUD icon visibility.

GetVehicleDisguiseState.doc: Returns disguise state given a table argument `{Player = uGuid}` — one of only two Player.* functions confirmed to take a table instead of positional arguments.

GetViewportId.doc: Given a player guid, returns the viewport id, used to bind GUI widgets to the correct split-screen viewport.

InCinematicMode.doc: Given a player guid, returns whether that player is currently in cinematic mode; used to gate input alongside checks like Object.IsAlive.

IsBoundaryDeath.doc: Given a character guid, returns whether being outside the boundary is currently set to be lethal for that character.

IsCoopMultiplayer.doc: Returns whether the game is in co-op multiplayer, called with no arguments, e.g. `if Player.IsCoopMultiplayer() then`.

IsLocal.doc: Given a player guid, returns whether that player is local, e.g. `Net.IsServer() and not Player.IsLocal(tData[1])`.

IsPositionOutBoundary.doc: Given a player guid and X/Y/Z coordinates, returns whether that position is outside the player's boundary; used in PDA map code.

IsRemote.doc: No confirmed call sites; presumed (unconfirmed) to be the inverse of IsLocal.

RemoveAllBoundary.doc: Removes all boundary zones registered for a player, given just a player guid.

RemoveBoundary.doc: Removes a specific boundary zone from a player, taking the same (uPlayerGuid, uBoundaryGuid) shape as AddBoundary.

RequestPDAMapModeCancel.doc: Requests cancellation of PDA map mode for a player, given just a player guid.

RequestPDAMapModeExit.doc: Requests exit of PDA map mode with a completion callback, e.g. `Player.RequestPDAMapModeExit(oMinigame:GetOwner(), _RemoveSatelliteTargettingMode, {oMinigame})`.

SetAimMode.doc: Enables/disables aim mode for a player, e.g. `Player.SetAimMode(Player.GetPrimaryPlayer(), true)`. Very common in real scripts.

SetAvailableCostumes.doc: Sets the count of available costumes; real call sites read from the WifPmcInterior resident-module getter and write into this engine setter, suggesting the two are kept in sync rather than sharing storage.

SetBoundaryCallback.doc: Registers a callback fired when a player crosses one of their registered boundary zones, e.g. `Player.SetBoundaryCallback(uPlayerGuid, BoundaryCallback)`.
