SetCash.doc: Sets cash to an exact amount. Confirmed working by live testing, but it skips the HUD refresh that MrxPmc.AddCashQty triggers, so the on-screen number won't visibly update — prefer MrxPmc.AddCashQty/GetCashQty unless you specifically want the silent low-level write.
SetCash.gotcha: Changes the underlying value but SKIPS the HUD refresh -- the number on screen doesn't update even though the cash really changed (confirmed live). Use MrxPmc.AddCashQty if you want the displayed value to move too.

SetCinematicMode.doc: Enables/disables cinematic mode for a player. Confirmed with a simple 2-argument form and richer forms with extra trailing arguments (e.g. bone-attach name, flags) that vary by call site — meaning beyond 'camera/cinematic attach parameters' is unconfirmed.
SetCinematicMode.gotcha: Required before per-tick Object.SetPosition changes visually propagate under a world-pause -- without it a prop's position can be set every frame and nothing moves on screen. It also steals control, so pair every enable with a guaranteed restore path.

SetFuel.doc: Sets fuel to an exact amount. Not directly exercised in live tests, but presumed to be the low-level setter behind MrxPmc.AddFuelQty/SetFuelCapacity; capacity generally needs to be raised before quantity when increasing fuel.

SetFuelCapacity.doc: Sets fuel capacity, taking an optional trailing flag: `(nCapacity [, bFlag])`. No direct call sites; presumed backing store for MrxPmc.SetFuelCapacity(nCapacity, bFlag) (real snippets call the wrapper as `MrxPmc.SetFuelCapacity(9999, true)`) — the argument shape is inferred, not independently confirmed.

SetGrappleEnabled.doc: Enables/disables grapple for a given guid, e.g. `Player.SetGrappleEnabled(uGuid, bEnable)`.

SetHealthClamp.doc: Enables/disables a health clamp for a player; paired with SetSurvivalMode in hero.lua.

SetInPmc.doc: Marks a player as inside/outside the PMC hub with a boolean, e.g. entering/leaving in wifpmcinterior.lua.

SetInputEnabled.doc: Enables/disables player input. Confirmed with both a 2-argument form `(uPlayerGuid, bEnable)` and a 3-argument form with a trailing boolean whose meaning is unconfirmed.

SetOutBoundary.doc: Sets/clears whether a player is currently registered as outside their boundary, e.g. `Player.SetOutBoundary(secondaryPlayer, true)`.

SetOutfit.doc: Given a character guid and a model-name string, sets that character's outfit/model; used by wardrobe code in wifpmcinterior.lua.

SetPDAMapMode.doc: Enables/disables PDA map mode with a long parameter list: player guid, enable flag, position, radius, min/max zoom deltas, and a minigame-use flag. Also called simply as `(uGuid, false)` to disable.

SetPDAMapModeCallback.doc: Registers a callback for PDA map mode transitions, e.g. `Player.SetPDAMapModeCallback(self.uOwner, true, SatelliteTargettingEnd, {self})`.

SetPDAMapModeCancelCallback.doc: Registers a callback fired when PDA map mode is cancelled, e.g. `Player.SetPDAMapModeCancelCallback(self.uOwner, SatelliteTargettingCancel, {self})`.

SetPlayerJoinedCallback.doc: Registers a callback for when a player joins. No confirmed call sites; presumed (unconfirmed) to follow the same callback-registration shape as Event.Create.

SetProfileCostume.doc: Sets the player's costume by index, e.g. `Player.SetProfileCostume(iIndex - 1)` — note real call sites apply a zero-based adjustment.

SetSatelliteScanMode.doc: Enables/disables satellite scan mode for a player at given coordinates, e.g. `Player.SetSatelliteScanMode(uPlayer, false, 0, 0, 0)`. Only the disable form (bEnable=false, zeroed coords) is attested; the enable form's coordinate meaning is unconfirmed.

SetScopeEnabled.doc: Enables/disables scope use for a player, e.g. `Player.SetScopeEnabled(Player.GetLocalPlayer(), false)`.

SetSeatMovementLocks.doc: Enables/disables seat movement locks for a player with a boolean, e.g. `Player.SetSeatMovementLocks(uPlayerGuid, true)`.

SetSurvivalMode.doc: Enables/disables survival mode for a player; paired with SetHealthClamp in hero.lua.

SetVehicleDisguise.doc: Enables/disables vehicle disguise with a single boolean, e.g. `Player.SetVehicleDisguise(bEnable)`.

TeleportCamera.doc: Given a player guid, snaps that player's camera to their current position, e.g. `Player.TeleportCamera(uSecondaryPlayer)` — used around co-op transitions.

VehicleDisguise.doc: Starts or removes a vehicle disguise change via a table argument: `{Player = uGuid, Callback = fCallback}` to start it (with a completion callback), or `{Player = uGuid, Remove = true}` to remove it.

GetCurrentLocalPlayers.doc: Returns the number of local players currently joined, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 (returned 1 at test time) -- the local-only counterpart to Player.GetCurrentPlayers.

GetLocalId.doc: Takes a local-player-slot index and returns that slot's id as a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier no-argument guess.
GetLocalId.gotcha: The argument is a slot index, not a uGuid, and 0-based vs 1-based indexing is unconfirmed -- test both 0 and 1 as the first slot. A bad index returns nil silently rather than erroring, as everywhere in this engine.

GetMaximumLocalPlayers.doc: Returns how many local/split-screen player slots this build supports, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 (returned 2).

GetOutBoundary.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to Player.SetOutBoundary.

GetProfileCharacter.doc: Returns the profile's selected character index for a local-player slot. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier no-argument guess.
GetProfileCharacter.gotcha: Takes the same local-player-slot idx as Player.GetLocalId/IsJoined, not a uGuid. Distinct from the no-argument Player.GetProfileCostume.

GetProfileUpgrade.doc: Returns a number for a local-player slot's profile upgrade state. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier bare-placeholder signature.
GetProfileUpgrade.gotcha: Takes the same local-player-slot idx as Player.GetLocalId/GetProfileCharacter, not a uGuid.

GetSeat.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Vehicle.GetSeatFromRider and Vehicle.GetFromRider cover similar ground from the vehicle side and do have real call sites -- prefer those.

GetViewport.doc: Returns 5 values for a local-player slot: width, height, x, y, and a fifth value of unconfirmed meaning (live example: 2560, 1440, 0, 0, 0). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- reach for it when positioning HUD elements against the real viewport.
GetViewport.gotcha: The argument is a local-player-slot index, not a uPlayerGuid as earlier guessed.

IsJoined.doc: Returns whether a local player is joined in a given slot, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
IsJoined.gotcha: The argument is the local-player-slot idx shared with Player.GetLocalId, not a uPlayerGuid as previously guessed.

SetPlayerStart.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed setter counterpart to Player.GetPlayerStart.

ActivateFactionRegionMusic.doc: Commits the current region's faction music; takes no arguments, called immediately after SetFactionMusic/LockFactionMusic(false).

AddCueToMusicSourcePlaylist.doc: Adds a music cue to a named source-music playlist.

AddFactionMusic.doc: Registers a faction or freeplay-name string with the faction-music system, during music-system init.

AddMusicSourcePlaylist.doc: Creates a source-music playlist given a playlist-name string and a numeric gap value.

AddMusicState.doc: Registers a named music state (e.g. "none", "explore", "action", "high_action", "hijack", "mission_success", etc) with 5 numeric parameters, during music-system init. Exact meaning of each numeric slot (duration/priority/fade-in/interval/fade-out are plausible guesses) is not confirmed.

AddMusicTransition.doc: Defines a legal transition edge between two already-registered music states plus 3 numeric parameters (meaning unconfirmed), building the state graph that TransitionMusic moves through.

AddSourceMusicEntryState.doc: Adds an entry state for source-music transitions. This is the newer API (used when `Sound._GetLibVersion() >= 11`) that replaces SetSourceMusicTransition.

BindMusicCue.doc: Binds a music cue name to a named music state.

ClearMusicCues.doc: Clears all cues bound to a named music state; typically followed immediately by a fresh BindMusicCue call.

ClearMusicSourcePlaylist.doc: Clears all cues from a named source-music playlist.

ClearSourceMusicEntryStates.doc: Clears source-music entry states; takes no arguments. Called immediately before AddSourceMusicEntryState, in the `>= 11` branch.

ClearSourceMusicTransitions.doc: Clears source-music transitions; takes no arguments. Called immediately before SetSourceMusicTransition, in the same `_GetLibVersion() < 11` fallback branch.

CueAmbience.doc: Starts an ambience stream given its stream name (single string argument).

CueSound.doc: Plays a sound cue on an object. Called with a real object uGuid for world sounds, or 0 for UI/HUD-attached one-shots; also commonly used directly as an Event.Create timer callback.
CueSound.gotcha: A real object guid attaches the sound to that object; nil/0 is the shipped convention for a positionless UI/HUD one-shot. Whichever you pass, Sound.StopSound needs the identical pair back or it won't stop it.

DefineReverbPreset.doc: Defines a reverb preset: an integer ID, a preset-name string, and a long run of further numeric DSP parameters (room size/decay/reflections/diffusion etc. are plausible by convention, but individual meanings aren't confirmed by the single call site observed).

FadeCategoryDown.doc: Fades a named mix category down to a given level over a given duration.

FadeCategoryUp.doc: Fades a named mix category back up over a given duration; the restore counterpart to FadeCategoryDown.

GetAudioDir.doc: Returns the audio directory path string; no arguments. Used to build sound-bank file paths.

IsDynamicMusic.doc: Returns whether dynamic music is currently enabled; no arguments. Used to snapshot the prior state before a temporary override.

IsFactionLockedMusic.doc: Returns whether faction music is currently locked; no arguments. Used to snapshot prior lock state before a temporary override.

LoadBankWithCallback.doc: Asynchronously loads a sound bank given a (localized) bank name and type string, invoking a completion callback function when done.

LoadTempBank.doc: Loads a temporary sound bank. A 4-argument variant of LoadBankWithCallback that also takes a callback-data table alongside the callback function.

LockActionLevelMusic.doc: Locks or unlocks the currently forced action level (boolean), typically paired with SetActionLevelsMusic to hold a forced level for a duration. Can be used directly as an Event.Create callback.

LockFactionMusic.doc: Locks or unlocks a forced faction-music selection with a boolean.

LockListenerPosition.doc: Locks or unlocks the audio listener's position with a boolean; used in matched pairs bracketing scripted camera/audio moments.

OpenStreamFile.doc: Opens a stream file given a stream name and a file name (two string arguments).

OverrideUserMusic.doc: Overrides the user's music selection; takes no arguments. Always called behind an `if Sound.OverrideUserMusic then` existence guard, paired with RestoreUserMusic as its counterpart.

PitchCategoryActivate.doc: Activates a pitch shift on a named category to a given level over a given duration.

PitchCategoryDeactivate.doc: Deactivates a pitch-shift category over a given duration; the restore counterpart to PitchCategoryActivate.

RegisterReadyCallback.doc: Registers a callback function that is invoked once the audio system finishes initializing.

RequestAmbienceBank.doc: Requests loading of an ambience sound bank, given a (localized) bank-name string.

RestoreUserMusic.doc: Restores the user's music selection after OverrideUserMusic; takes no arguments, called behind the same existence-guard pattern as its counterpart.

SetActionLevelsMusic.doc: Forces/raises the current music action level. First numeric argument varies by call site (observed 0, 3, 10, 15); the meaning of the trailing 3 numeric args (always 0 in observed calls) is unconfirmed.

SetActionThresholdsMusic.doc: Sets action-level thresholds for a named music state plus 2 numeric arguments. Only the state names "none" and "explore" are seen at any call site.

SetDynamicMusic.doc: Enables or disables the dynamic music system with a single boolean.

SetFactionMusic.doc: Sets/selects the current faction whose music should play, by faction-name string.

SetHijackMusic.doc: Registers which music states back hijack-success/resume music, given two state-name strings, during init only. It does not itself start hijack music — actual hijack-time music is triggered separately via Sound.TransitionMusic("hijack") in mrxsound.lua's BeginActionHijack/EndActionHijack.

SetMasterVolume.doc: Sets the master volume level (observed values 0 and 1) with a fade duration in seconds as the second argument.

SetReverb.doc: Sets reverb by integer ID; used as a fallback alongside SetReverbPreset.

SetReverbPreset.doc: Sets the active reverb preset, accepting either the preset's name string or its integer ID interchangeably, gated by a version/feature check between the two call forms.

SetRootFactionRegionMusic.doc: Sets the root faction/region used for faction-region music, by faction-name string; called once during music-system init.

SetSourceMusic.doc: Sets the "source" music state name used by the source-music playlist system, during music-system init.

SetSourceMusicTransition.doc: Sets entry/exit state names for source-music transitions. Used only in a fallback code path when `Sound._GetLibVersion() < 11` (the older API, superseded by AddSourceMusicEntryState).

SetSurvivalMode.doc: Enables/disables survival-mode audio state with a boolean; paired with CueSound/StopSound of the "sfx_survival_lp" loop in the same functions.

SetTimerUpdateMusic.doc: Toggles timer-driven music updates with a boolean; observed toggled around timer-critical gameplay such as mission countdowns.

SetVehicleEngineBoost.doc: Sets a vehicle's engine-boost sound state for the given vehicle uGuid and a numeric level (observed values 0 and 1). Always called behind an existence guard, same late-addition pattern as StopAndFlushAllSounds.

StopAmbience.doc: Stops an ambience stream previously started with CueAmbience, using the same stream name.

StopAndFlushAllSounds.doc: Stops and flushes all currently playing sounds; takes no arguments. Always called behind an `if Sound.StopAndFlushAllSounds then` existence guard, implying it was added in a later game build than some calling code.

StopSound.doc: Stops a sound cue previously started with CueSound, using the same (uGuid, sCueName) pair. Also used with uGuid 0 to stop UI/HUD sounds.
StopSound.gotcha: Must be called with the SAME (uGuidOrNil, sCueName) pair the original Sound.CueSound used -- a mismatched guid (including passing nil where 0 was used, or vice versa) silently fails to stop anything.

TransitionMusic.doc: The actual trigger that moves the dynamic music state machine to a named, already-registered state (e.g. "hijack", "action", "mission_success"). Takes an optional trailing boolean flag whose meaning is unconfirmed.

UnloadBankWithCallback.doc: Asynchronously unloads a sound bank; same (sBankName, sType, funcCallback) argument shape as LoadBankWithCallback.

UnloadTempBank.doc: Unloads a temporary sound bank; same (sBankName, sType, funcCallback, tCallbackData) shape as LoadTempBank.

_GetLibVersion.doc: Returns the audio engine's build/version number (integer, no arguments). Used repeatedly in real scripts as a feature-gate, e.g. `if Sound._GetLibVersion() >= 11 then` to choose between older and newer music/reverb APIs. Leading underscore suggests an internal accessor, but it is genuinely used by shipped code.

AddFadeCategory.doc: Registers a sound category for fading. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Sound.FadeCategoryUp/FadeCategoryDown.

AddPitchCategory.doc: Registers a sound category for pitch control. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Sound.PitchCategoryActivate/PitchCategoryDeactivate.

CloseStreamFile.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Sound.OpenStreamFile, by naming only.

ForceActionTransition.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a forced variant of Sound.TransitionMusic restricted to action-level states, by naming only.

GetMaxDuration.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus.
GetMaxDuration.gotcha: The cue-name signature is guessed purely from the name (a cue-length query), not from any observed call.

IsActionLevelLockedMusic.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed the getter counterpart to Sound.LockActionLevelMusic, by naming only.

LoadBank.doc: Loads a sound bank by name and type. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Sound.LoadBankWithCallback/LoadTempBank.

LoadSoundBank.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus.
LoadSoundBank.gotcha: Sound.LoadBankWithCallback and Sound.LoadTempBank are the confirmed loading entry points actually used by real scripts; this may be a lower-level or type-specific variant, but that is inference, not evidence.

PauseSound.doc: Pauses a cue playing on an object. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to Sound.CueSound/StopSound.

RemoveMusicSourcePlaylist.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to Sound.AddMusicSourcePlaylist, by naming only.

SetCategoryPitch.doc: Sets the pitch for a sound category. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Sound.PitchCategoryActivate.

SetCategoryVolume.doc: Sets the volume for a sound category. No call sites in the corpus -- the signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Sound.FadeCategoryUp/FadeCategoryDown.

SetSourceEnterMusic.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed related to Sound.SetSourceMusic/SetSourceExitMusic by naming only.

SilenceAmbience.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a mute/duck variant distinct from Sound.StopAmbience, by naming only.

TestCueSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The Test prefix suggests a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.CueSound.

TestPauseSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.PauseSound, by naming only.

TestStopSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.StopSound, by naming only.

UnloadBank.doc: Unloads a sound bank by name and type. No call sites in the corpus -- presumed the synchronous counterpart to Sound.LoadBank, by naming only.

_SummonEd.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The leading underscore matches this codebase's private/internal convention; "Ed" plausibly names an internal editor or debug-visualisation hook, but the name is the only clue available.

AutoLoad.doc: Returns a boolean used as a gate to skip the shell/menu flow and auto-load directly into the game; called with no arguments.

FinishedShell.doc: Returns whether the shell has finished; called defensively (`if Sys.FinishedShell and Sys.FinishedShell() then`), suggesting it may not exist on every build.

ForceNextAutosave.doc: Forces the next autosave to occur; called with no arguments.
ForceNextAutosave.gotcha: The second Lua-reachable autosave choke point; gating only Sys.RequestAutosave leaves this path open. Stash the original rather than discarding it so a deliberate re-enable stays possible.

GetAssetRequestMax.doc: Returns the maximum number of concurrent asset requests; used both to cache the original throttle value and as a comparison bound against pending asset operations.

GetCharacterTemplate.doc: Returns a character-template name string; used as a fallback in a chain ending in the hardcoded default `"mattias"`.

GetForceNewGame.doc: Returns whether a new game should be forced; called defensively (`if Sys.GetForceNewGame and Sys.GetForceNewGame() then`).

GetINIBriefing.doc: Returns a boolean INI-briefing setting; called with no arguments, widely used in shell/briefing flow.

GetLanguage.doc: Returns the current language as a string; can return nil/falsy on some builds — the one confirmed call site uses an `or "English"` fallback.

GetLevelName.doc: Returns the current level name as a string; called with no arguments, very widely used (including compared/lower-cased at call sites).

GetMasterScriptName.doc: Returns the master script name string; used alongside GetLevelName to drive Net.StartServer(...) and LevelBootstrap.LoadLevel(...) calls.

GetPlatform.doc: Returns a numeric platform ID (treated as a number at the call site, not a string); called with no arguments.

GetShellCode.doc: Returns the shell code string; called with no arguments.

GetSkipMission.doc: Returns the mission name to skip to, as a string; called with no arguments.

GetVersion.doc: Returns two values, `sCode, sData = Sys.GetVersion()`, describing the build version.

GuidToString.doc: Converts a GUID handle (`uGuid`) to its string form. Very widely used, often as a table key (e.g. hashing a state/node name) or for debug printing.
GuidToString.gotcha: Confirmed to THROW on some objects rather than returning nil -- pcall it. Unprotected calls to this (and Object.GetName) were the root cause of a tool whose whole timer chain silently died after one entry.

HaveActiveProfile.doc: Called with no arguments, presumably to check for an active save profile; its return value is discarded at the only confirmed call site, so its actual use is unconfirmed.

IsConfirmOnCircle.doc: Returns whether the confirm button follows the PlayStation-style 'circle to cancel' convention rather than 'cross to confirm' — a region/platform-specific controller setting. Very widely used, almost always called guarded (`if Sys.IsConfirmOnCircle and ...`).

IsDemoMode.doc: Returns whether the build is running in demo mode; called defensively (`if Sys.IsDemoMode and Sys.IsDemoMode() then`).

IsFinalConfig.doc: Returns whether this is a final (non-debug) build; called defensively, used to gate a debug-only skip button so it's unavailable in final builds.

IsGermanSKU.doc: Returns whether this is the German SKU; called unguarded (unlike most other Is* queries on this page) to gate region-specific content, presumably gore/violence toggles for the German release.

IsLoadingOrStreaming.doc: Returns whether the game is currently loading or streaming assets; called defensively, used to skip certain per-frame logic while loading.

LTIGetPrecacheBypass.doc: Returns a number (not a plain boolean) indicating precache-bypass state; compared against 0 (`if Sys.LTIGetPrecacheBypass() > 0 then`) to decide whether to bypass LTI precaching.

MainTime.doc: Returns the current time with no arguments, used as a fallback session-time source. Presumed to be the engine's internal pausable/scaled clock in seconds, paired with MainTimeStamp; whether it pauses or is affected by SetTimeScale is unconfirmed.

MainTimeStamp.doc: Captures a timestamp handle used the same way as RealTimeStamp (e.g. for session/task timers). Presumed tied to the engine's internal pausable/scaled 'main' clock rather than a real-world clock, though the exact difference from RealTimeStamp is unconfirmed.
MainTimeStamp.gotcha: The PAUSABLE/scaled clock -- it tracks Sys.SetTimeScale and game pause, so a timer built on it stalls in menus. Use Sys.RealTimeStamp for UI or real-world timing that must not freeze.

NoHud.doc: Returns whether the HUD should be hidden; called unguarded to gate HUD-manager update logic.

PlayIntroMovies.doc: Returns whether intro movies should play; used to gate movie playback during bootstrap.

RealTimeStamp.doc: Captures a real-world-clock timestamp handle with no arguments, e.g. `uLockTimer = Sys.RealTimeStamp()`, later read via Sys.TimeStampGetElapsed().
RealTimeStamp.gotcha: The REAL-WORLD clock -- it keeps advancing through pause and slow-mo. That's what you want for UI/wall-clock timing, but it makes a gameplay cooldown built on it keep ticking while the player sits in a menu; use Sys.MainTimeStamp for anything that should freeze with the game.

RequestAutosave.doc: Requests an autosave: `Sys.RequestAutosave(bInMission, bLastMission, fMissionTime, nPercentCompleted)`. Sometimes called defensively (checked for existence first), suggesting it may be an optional/late-bound entry point not present on every build.
RequestAutosave.gotcha: One of only TWO Lua-reachable autosave choke points -- no-op'ing this one alone still lets Sys.ForceNextAutosave write an experimental world state into the player's real save. Suppress both, before any layer/attitude/transit change, not after.

RequestGameState.doc: Requests a game-state transition given a free-form state-name string, e.g. "Shell", "ingame", "cinematic", "Pause", "Loading", "WaitForTether", "PDA". This is the core state-transition entry point, used dozens of times across shell/bootstrap code; state names aren't enumerated as constants anywhere, and it can return a success boolean.
RequestGameState.gotcha: State names are free-form strings with no constants anywhere -- a typo is not an error, it just doesn't transition. Requesting "WaitForStreaming" is what actually composites a pending layer change, and it must be paired with a matching MrxState.Exit or the screen stays faded to black.

RequiredAsset.doc: Registers an asset as required for the current level: `Sys.RequiredAsset(sAssetName, sAssetType, nPriority, bFlag)`. Confirmed for both "layer" and "script" asset types with a negative priority in both observed cases; the trailing boolean's meaning is not confirmed.

RumbleEnabled.doc: Returns whether controller rumble is enabled; read as part of the pause-screen options-menu system settings.

SetAssetRequestMax.doc: Sets the maximum number of concurrent asset requests: `Sys.SetAssetRequestMax(nMax)`. Used by the layer manager to temporarily raise the asset-streaming throttle and later restore the original value.

SetINIBriefing.doc: Sets the INI-briefing boolean setting: `Sys.SetINIBriefing(bValue)`. Confirmed used to toggle it via `SetINIBriefing(not GetINIBriefing())`.

SetLuaSaveVersion.doc: Sets the Lua save-data version: `Sys.SetLuaSaveVersion(nVersion)`. Always called once during bootstrap with the return value of a local GetSaveDataVersion() helper.

SetNumberOfViewports.doc: Sets the number of active viewports: `Sys.SetNumberOfViewports(n)`; confirmed called with 1.

SetSkipMission.doc: Sets the mission to skip to by name: `Sys.SetSkipMission(sMissionName)`; also confirmed called with an empty string to clear it.

SetTimeScale.doc: Sets the game's global time scale: `Sys.SetTimeScale(nScale)`. Confirmed used for a slow-motion-style effect, with the scale clamped to a minimum value before being applied.

SetTutorialsEnabled.doc: Sets whether tutorials are enabled: `Sys.SetTutorialsEnabled(bEnable)`. Setter counterpart to TutorialsEnabled; called defensively (checked for existence first) from the tutorials options-menu toggle.

StartSingleplayer.doc: Starts a singleplayer session given a level name and master script name: `Sys.StartSingleplayer(sLevelName, sMasterScript)`.

StartWithResources.doc: Returns whether to start with resources; called defensively (`if Sys.StartWithResources and Sys.StartWithResources() then`).

StringToGuid.doc: Converts a GUID string (e.g. a "0x..." hex string) to a GUID handle. Very likely the same underlying function as the bare global `StringToGuid` used pervasively elsewhere in the corpus, though the aliasing evidence is one-directional — strong for StringToGuid, unconfirmed for GuidToString.

SubtitlesEnabled.doc: Returns whether subtitles are enabled; used both guarded and unguarded, read in the pause-screen options menu.

TimeStampGetElapsed.doc: Returns elapsed seconds since a timestamp handle (from MainTimeStamp/RealTimeStamp, re-markable via TimeStampMark) was last marked. Forms a poll-based elapsed-time primitive, an alternative to the callback-based Event.TimerRelative for code that needs to check elapsed time on demand.

TimeStampMark.doc: Resets/re-marks an existing timestamp handle in place. Call sites consistently re-mark a stamp previously produced by MainTimeStamp/RealTimeStamp rather than creating a new one.

TutorialsEnabled.doc: Returns whether the tutorial-hint HUD message system is enabled. This is the gate checked in MrxTutorialManager before showing or updating a tutorial popup message, and it's read defensively in the pause-screen options-menu toggle.

YAxisInverted.doc: Returns whether the Y-axis is inverted; read alongside RumbleEnabled/SubtitlesEnabled in the same pause-screen options read.

Clock.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Clock.gotcha: What the number means is still unconfirmed -- raw tick count versus clock-seconds was never settled.

Date.doc: Returns the current date and time as a string in MM/DD/YY HH:MM:SS format, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Date.gotcha: Unlike its numeric Time & Clock siblings, this one returns a formatted string, not a number.

DiffTime.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed to compute a difference between two time values by naming, unconfirmed.

IsAutosaveEnabled.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to Sys.SetAutosaveEnabled, unconfirmed.

MemUsage.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number, confirming the presumed memory-diagnostics role. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

RealTime.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; consistent with the presumed real-world-clock counterpart to Sys.MainTime, paired with Sys.RealTimeStamp.
RealTime.gotcha: The unit and epoch are unconfirmed -- only that a number comes back.

Time.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; the probe found Sys.Time, Sys.RealTime and Sys.Clock all returning the same number shape, with no way yet to tell them apart.

ToStringL.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a localised/long string conversion by naming, unconfirmed.

WriteToConsole.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug-console print by naming, unconfirmed.

Send.doc: Opens a TCP connection, writes sMsg, and closes it.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine. LOOPBACK ONLY: the implementation blocks any destination outside 127.0.0.0/8 and returns without sending, deliberately, so an untrusted script cannot port-scan your network or exfiltrate data. A send to a non-local host fails SILENTLY -- there is no error, so check the host first if nothing arrives. Ports and the message are capped (host 128 bytes, message 2048).

CancelHijack.doc: Takes a plain character guid; cancels an active hijack. Observed being called on player logout/cleanup.

ClearControls.doc: Takes a plain vehicle guid; clears the vehicle's controls, called alongside turret-disable logic during hijack setup.

CloseDoor.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a door/part name string (e.g. "pivot"); mirrors OpenDoor to close it.

EnableTurret.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, a turret/part name ("head", "main_turret"), a boolean, and sometimes an axis string ("pitch", "all") plus another boolean. Confirmed to be control/orientation-only, not weapon selection: every real call site just disables or re-enables the turret's own control during a hijack cinematic and never touches what the turret fires.

Enter.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, character guid, a seat-type string ("d", "p"), and one or two boolean flags (immediate, plus an optional extra flag). Puts a character into a vehicle by seat type rather than a specific seat guid.

EnterBySeatGuid.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, character guid, seat guid, and one or two boolean flags (immediate, plus an extra flag); returns a success boolean. Puts a character into a specific seat identified by guid.

Exit.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a character guid, frequently with a trailing boolean flag; removes the character from the vehicle.

GetDriver.doc: Returns the driver's character guid for a vehicle uGuid, or nil if unmanned. Very widely used in real game scripts, often guarded with a nil check.

GetFromRider.doc: Takes a character uGuid; returns the vehicle guid the character is currently riding in, or nil if the character is on foot.

GetRiders.doc: Takes a vehicle uGuid and an optional seat-type filter string (e.g. "p", "g", "driver"); returns a table of rider guids.

GetSeatByType.doc: Takes a vehicle uGuid and a seat-type string ("p", "d"); at least one real call site passes a third boolean argument as well.

GetSeatFromRider.doc: Takes a character uGuid; returns the guid of the seat that character occupies.

GetSeatParams.doc: Takes a seat guid; returns a params table that includes at least an IsGunner field per observed usage.

GetSeatToSeat.doc: Takes a seat guid and a boolean; appears to return possible seat-transfer targets from that seat.

HijackAbort.doc: Takes a plain character (hijacker) guid. Part of the hijack state machine; aborts an in-progress hijack.

HijackAbortDone.doc: Takes a plain character (hijacker) guid. Part of the hijack state machine; signals that a hijack-abort has finished.

HijackComplete.doc: Takes a plain character (hijacker) guid. Part of the hijack state machine; signals a successful hijack completion.

HijackStart.doc: Takes a hijacker guid, hijackee guid, vehicle guid, and (in the one observed call site) a fourth argument that was a table/object reference (self). Begins the hijack state machine.

IsFlying.doc: Takes a plain vehicle guid; returns a boolean, checked before flight-specific hijack logic runs.

IsHijackRemote.doc: Takes a character guid; checks whether a hijack is remote. Its one real call site guards the call itself with `Vehicle.IsHijackRemote and ...`, implying the function's presence was historically uncertain in some contexts.

IsSeatALadder.doc: Takes a plain seat guid; returns a boolean for whether that seat is a ladder-type seat.

IsSeatBlocked.doc: Takes a plain seat guid; returns a boolean for whether the seat is currently blocked/unusable.

OpenDoor.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a door/part name string (e.g. "pivot", "DriverHatch"). Using it to open a tank hatch ("DriverHatch") has been proposed as a live test but is not yet confirmed working.

SetCanPlayerUse.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, a seat-type string ("d", "a"), and a boolean; controls whether a player can use that seat type.

SetHijackState.doc: Takes a character guid and a numeric state value; sets the hijacker's state within the hijack state machine (exact state numbering not documented from call sites).

SetHijackSuccess.doc: Takes a character guid and a boolean (observed as false in the corpus); records hijack success/failure for that character.

SetParts.doc: Takes a vehicle/object guid, a part name string (e.g. "LightFront", "CtrlRotation"), and a boolean; returns a boolean. Also seen used on non-vehicle gate/alarm objects, suggesting broader applicability than just player vehicles.

SetTurretPitch.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, turret name, and a numeric pitch value (observed as 0, resetting pitch to level right after disabling the turret during hijack). Orientation only, same caveat as EnableTurret — does not affect firing.

StopTankHijackMotion.doc: Takes a plain vehicle guid; stops the tank hijack motion/animation sequence.

TransferToSeat.doc: Takes a vehicle guid, a seat guid, and a boolean flag; transfers a rider between seats.

Usable.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a boolean; toggles whether the vehicle can be entered/used at all.

GetFromSeat.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a seat identifier. Live-probed 2026-07-22 and inconclusive: neither 'd' (string) nor 0 (number) as the seat argument returned anything but nil.
GetFromSeat.gotcha: Not a working call yet -- the correct seat-id shape is unconfirmed. Try a seat guid from Vehicle.GetSeatByType/GetSeatToSeat rather than a guessed literal.

GetRiderFromSeat.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a seat identifier; presumed the inverse of Vehicle.GetSeatFromRider by naming symmetry. Live-probed 2026-07-22 with the same inconclusive result as Vehicle.GetFromSeat.
GetRiderFromSeat.gotcha: Neither 'd' nor 0 as the seat argument returned anything but nil -- the correct seat-id shape is still unconfirmed.

IsFlipped.doc: Returns whether a vehicle is flipped over, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the corpus.

IsHijackBad.doc: Returns a boolean about hijack viability. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
IsHijackBad.gotcha: The probe did not disambiguate which guid it expects -- hijacker character or vehicle. Naming symmetry with the adjacent uHijacker-taking hijack functions makes the hijacker likelier, but that is inference.

RestoreAmmo.doc: Refills a vehicle's ammo. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 as a write with no return value; still no call sites in the corpus.

RestoreHealth.doc: Heals a vehicle to full health -- confirmed live 2026-07-22 (98.9 to 100 in the probe). A write with no return value.

SetTurretYaw.doc: Sets a vehicle turret's yaw from a numeric angle. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 as a write with no return value.
SetTurretYaw.gotcha: Presumed analogous to the confirmed Vehicle.SetTurretPitch by naming only -- including whether it is orientation-only, which this probe did not re-verify.

GetMaxReserveAmmo.doc: Returns the maximum reserve ammo capacity for a carried weapon guid (uWeapon). Almost always paired with SetReserveAmmo in the idiom Weapon.SetReserveAmmo(uWeapon, Weapon.GetMaxReserveAmmo(uWeapon)) to refill a weapon to full.

GetReserveAmmo.doc: Returns the current reserve ammo count for a carried/equipped weapon guid (uWeapon). Always called with a player's hand-held weapon, never a vehicle weapon.

SetReserveAmmo.doc: Sets the reserve ammo of a carried weapon guid (uWeapon) to nAmount. Commonly used to refill a weapon to max via Weapon.SetReserveAmmo(uWeapon, Weapon.GetMaxReserveAmmo(uWeapon)), but is also seen setting a flat value like 1; it can also be registered directly as an Event.Create callback (e.g. for ObjectHibernation), so it may be invoked by the engine's event dispatcher rather than called directly.

sin.doc: Sine of x, in RADIANS.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine. Shipped in v0.1.6 -- the Taylor-series CustomSin fallback older wiki snippets carry predates this and is no longer needed.

cos.doc: Cosine of x, in RADIANS.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine. Shipped in v0.1.6, same as math.sin.

tan.doc: Tangent of x, in radians.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine. New in v0.2.0.

asin.doc: Arc sine, returning radians.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

acos.doc: Arc cosine, returning radians.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

atan.doc: Arc tangent, returning radians. For a full-circle angle from a vector use math.atan2(y, x) instead.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

atan2.doc: Arc tangent of y/x using the signs of both to pick the correct quadrant -- the one to use for a heading from a direction vector. Note the argument order is (y, x), not (x, y).  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

sinh.doc: Hyperbolic sine.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

cosh.doc: Hyperbolic cosine.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

tanh.doc: Hyperbolic tangent.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

sqrt.doc: Square root. Ess.Raw and most distance maths use it; before v0.2.0 scripts had to hand-roll one.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

log.doc: Natural logarithm (base e).  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

log10.doc: Base-10 logarithm.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

fmod.doc: Floating-point remainder of x/y, keeping x's sign -- not the same as Lua's % operator for negative x.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

ldexp.doc: Returns m * 2^e.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

modf.doc: Splits x into its integral and fractional parts, returning both.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

frexp.doc: Splits x into a normalised mantissa and an exponent, so that x = m * 2^e.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

random.doc: Stock Lua 5.1 semantics: random() gives a float in [0,1), random(n) an integer in [1,n], random(m,n) an integer in [m,n].  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine. NOT the same function as the engine's own math.randf(), which the decompiled game scripts use -- the two are independent RNGs living side by side and neither replaces the other.
random.gotcha: This is a lua-bridge POLYFILL (v0.2.0+) and is a completely different function from the engine's own Math.randf -- the two are independent RNGs living side by side and neither reseeds or replaces the other. Seeding one does nothing to the other.

randomseed.doc: Seeds the generator used by math.random. Does not affect the engine's separate math.randf().  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

pi.doc: CONSTANT, not a function: 3.14159... Injected by a Lua polyfill chunk, because luaL_register can only register functions.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

huge.doc: CONSTANT, not a function: positive infinity, the standard Lua 5.1 sentinel for 'no maximum'.  Added by lua-bridge, not the engine.

MrxFactionManager.doc: Manages faction relations, attitudes, the attitude meter, reporting/pursuit (civilians calling you in) and civilian-casualty charges. It is always resident and importable from anywhere, which is why the networking and co-op-chat deep dives hijack its NetEventCallback to carry their own custom net events. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxFactionManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxFactionManager' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Initializes attitude level mappings and faction template to abbreviation mappings. It populates _tAttitudeLevelsToLabels and _tAttitudeLabelsToLevels based on _tAttitudes, and assigns unique GUIDs to each faction in _tFactions.

Reset.doc: Resets the report system by initializing it with default parameters.

Setup.doc: Sets up the report system, initializes pursuit level times, and configures various aspects of faction management. It also sets up next flybys, achievements, disguise handling, faction zone handling, and HUD faction display thresholds.

SendPlayerJoinEvents.doc: Sends network events to synchronize mutable factions and civilian casualties when a player joins the game.

GetFactionStringIndex.doc: Retrieves the faction abbreviation based on a string hash. Returns "NO NAME" if no matching faction is found.

NetEventCallback.doc: Handles network events related to faction management. It processes mutable factions and civilian casualties based on the event ID.

NetInitializeClientFactionRelations.doc: Initializes client-side faction relations in a staggered manner to avoid performance issues.

SetAttitudeMutable.doc: Marks a faction's attitude as mutable, adds it to the HUD attitude meter and initialises its relation with PMC, sending a net event when done on the server. Call this before trying to change a faction's standing.
SetAttitudeMutable.gotcha: This is the fix for SetRelation silently doing nothing on a faction that is not yet mutable.

IsAttitudeMutable.doc: Checks if a faction's attitude is mutable by returning the boolean value stored in _tFactions.

CanAttitudeBeMutable.doc: Checks if the attitude of a faction with the given abbreviation (sAbbrev) can be dynamically changed. Returns boolean: True if the attitude is mutable, false otherwise.

GetRelation.doc: Retrieves the relation value between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The relation value between the two factions.

TestAttitude.doc: Tests if the attitude between two factions meets a specified comparison condition against a given attitude label. Returns boolean: True if the condition is met, false otherwise.

GetAttitudeLevel.doc: Retrieves the attitude level between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The attitude level between the two factions.

GetAttitudeLabel.doc: Retrieves the attitude label between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns string: The attitude label between the two factions.

GetMeterValue.doc: Retrieves the meter value representing the attitude between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The meter value representing the attitude.

GetPriceScale.doc: Retrieves the price scale factor based on the attitude between two factions. Returns number: The price scale factor.

SetRelation.doc: Sets the relation value between two factions and updates related UI elements and events.
SetRelation.gotcha: Confirmed working by live testing — with a real gotcha: silently no-ops toward "Pmc" if the subject faction isn't currently mutable.

ChangeRelation.doc: Changes the relation value between two factions by a specified amount.

CreateAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Creates a non-persistent attitude change event with specified parameters and callback.

CreatePersistentAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Creates a persistent attitude change event with specified parameters and callback.

_CreateAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Internal function to create an attitude change event, either persistent or non-persistent.

ConvertRelationToMeterValue.doc: Converts a relation value to a meter value representing attitude. Returns number: The converted meter value.

ConvertRelationToAttitudeLevel.doc: Converts a relation value to an attitude level based on defined ranges. Returns number: The corresponding attitude level.

GetAttitudeFromLevel.doc: Retrieves the attitude label from a given attitude level. Returns string: The corresponding attitude label.

GetFactionAbbrevs.doc: Retrieves a sorted list of all faction abbreviations. Returns table: A table containing the sorted faction abbreviations.

GetFactionAbbrev.doc: Converts a faction template name into its short abbreviation ("All", "Chi", "Gur", ...), which is the form the rest of this module's API expects. Commonly fed the full-name string returned by MrxUtil.GetFaction.

GetFactionAbbrevFromFactionGuid.doc: Retrieves the abbreviation for a faction based on its GUID. Returns string: The corresponding faction abbreviation.

GetFactionTemplateName.doc: Retrieves the template name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The corresponding faction template name.

GetBribableFactions.doc: Retrieves a list of factions that can be bribed based on their attitude towards the PMC and mutability. Returns table: A table containing the abbreviations of bribe-able factions.

GetAttitudes.doc: Retrieves a table mapping attitude labels to their median values. Returns table: A table where keys are attitude labels and values are their median values.

GetAttitudeMedianValue.doc: Retrieves the median value for a given attitude label. Returns number: The median value of the attitude.

GetRgbColor.doc: Retrieves the RGB color associated with the attitude between two factions. Returns table: A table containing the RGB color values.

SaveSingleton.doc: Saves the current state of faction relations and mutable factions for persistence. Returns table: A table containing saved data including relations, mutable factions, civilian casualties, and penalties.

LoadSingleton.doc: Loads the saved state of faction relations and mutable factions from provided save data.

GetPlayerVisibleName.doc: Retrieves the player-visible name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The player-visible name of the faction.

GetShortPlayerVisibleName.doc: Retrieves the short player-visible name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The short player-visible name of the faction.

GetAdjective.doc: Retrieves the adjective associated with a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The adjective for the faction.

GetInlineIcon.doc: Retrieves the inline icon texture for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The inline icon texture name.

GetMarkerTexture.doc: Retrieves the marker texture for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The marker texture name.

CivCasualtySetup.doc: Sets up event handling for civilian casualties, initializing a persistent event to resolve civilian deaths.

ResolveCivCasualty.doc: Resolves the consequences of a civilian death, including determining if it was caused by the player and charging penalties.

ChargeCivCasualty.doc: Charges penalties for civilian casualties, updates player statistics, and triggers related events and voice cues.

GetFactionStringAbbrev.doc: Retrieves the faction abbreviation string for a given GUID and optional hash. If uAbbrev is provided, it searches _tFactions for a matching hash; otherwise, it calls GetFactionAbbrev(GetFaction(uGuid)).

NetSafeRemoveReportingDisplay.doc: Safely removes the reporting display by calling GetFactionStringAbbrev to get the faction abbreviation and then invoking RemoveReportingDisplay.

NetSafeHandleReporter0.doc: Handles reporter state 0 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter0.

NetSafeHandleReporter1.doc: Handles reporter state 1 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter1.

NetSafeHandleReporter2.doc: Handles reporter state 2 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter2.

NetSafeFinishedReporting.doc: Safely finishes reporting by getting the faction abbreviation and calling FinishedReporting.

RemoveReportingDisplay.doc: Removes the reporting display for a given GUID and faction abbreviation. It removes markers, halts pulses, deletes minimap objectives, and cancels timers if specified.

HandleReporter0.doc: Handles reporter state 0 by setting up markers, radar objectives, and voice sequences based on the faction data. It also starts a timer if necessary and sends a network message if on the server.

HandleTressPasser.doc: Handles tresspassers by playing voice-over messages and setting timers. It checks if a VO has already been played to avoid repetition.

HandleReporter1.doc: Handles reporter state 1 by checking for jamming conditions, starting timers, and playing voice sequences based on faction data. It also updates the network state if on the server.

HandleReporter2.doc: Handles reporter state 2 by removing reporting displays, updating active reporters, and setting report delays. It also updates the network state if on the server.

AmIBeingJammed.doc: Checks if a given GUID is being jammed by comparing factions of drivers in vehicles with AA levels.

HandleReporter.doc: Handles different reporter states (0, 1, 2) by calling appropriate functions based on the current state.

ValidateReporter.doc: Validates a reporter by checking faction mutability, disabled reporters, and other conditions. Logs reasons for cancellation if validation fails.

FinishedReporting.doc: Handles the completion of reporting by adjusting relations, setting delays, incrementing pursuits if necessary, playing voice sequences, posting events, and updating network states.

expand.doc: Expands a table by printing each entry's index and values. This function is defined twice in this part.

SetReportDelay.doc: Sets the report delay for various factions based on the provided delay value.

GetFaction.doc: Retrieves the faction label for a given GUID from a predefined list of factions. Logs an error if no faction label is found.

GetPerceivedFaction.doc: Gets the perceived faction by checking if the object is disguised and retrieving the faction accordingly.

DisableReporter.doc: Disables a reporter by setting its GUID in tDisabledReporters and handling active reporters.

EnableReporter.doc: Enables a reporter by removing its GUID from tDisabledReporters.

DisableReporting.doc: Disables or enables reporting based on the input boolean bDisable. If reporting is disabled, it logs "Reporting DISABLED" and handles any active reporter.

SetFactionReporting.doc: Sets the reporting status for a specific faction (sFaction). Logs whether the faction was found and updates its bCanReport field in _tFactions.

IncrementPursuit.doc: Increments the pursuit level for a given faction abbreviation. It retrieves the faction's GUID, adjusts the pursuit level to a maximum of 3, sets the pursuit duration, starts the pursuit on the HUD, and optionally plays a voice-over cue if available.

LockPursuit.doc: Locks the pursuit for a specific faction identified by uGuid at a given nLevel. It updates the pursuit state in Pg, starts the pursuit display on the HUD, and hides any meters for factions.

ClearPursuitLock.doc: Clears all pursuit locks. It hides meters for all factions and clears the pursuit lock in Pg.

SetCustomPursuit.doc: Sets a custom pursuit for a specific faction with a given duration and settings. It updates the pursuit state in Pg, starts the pursuit display on the HUD, and hides any meters for factions.

ClearCustomPursuit.doc: Clears all custom pursuits. It hides meters for all factions and clears the custom pursuit in Pg.

RandomFlyby.doc: Generates a random flyby based on faction configurations defined in tFlybys. It selects a random faction, template, and number of aircraft to spawn, calculates positions, and triggers the flyby using Airstrike.Flyby.

SetupNextFlyby.doc: Sets up a timer for the next random flyby. It creates an event that triggers RandomFlyby after a random interval between 19 and 90 seconds.

GetPdaFactionIdFromFactionId.doc: Retrieves the PDA faction ID from a given faction ID by looking up _tFactions.

GetFactionIdFromIndex.doc: Retrieves the faction ID at a specific index in _tFactions.

GetIndexFromFactionId.doc: Retrieves the index of a specific faction ID in _tFactions.

MrxGui.doc: Top-level GUI facade. Its Init() copies the widget classes and widget-management functions out of MrxGuiBase (plus the dialog- and numeric-box entry points) into the MrxGui namespace, which is why HUD code everywhere calls MrxGui.ImageWidget:new() / MrxGui.AddWidget(...). On top of that aliasing it natively implements global screen fades, HUD messages, the objective-description callback and the E3 demo-mode toggle. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGui") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGui' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Init() binds these MrxGui.* names to their real implementations: - Widget classes (call :new() on these): Widget, ImageWidget, TextWidget, FlashWidget, SpriteWidget, MovieWidget, MinimapWidget ← MrxGuiBase.*. - Widget management: AddWidget, AddWidgetWithChildren, RemoveWidget, RemoveWidgetWithChildren, RemoveEverySingleWidget (← MrxGuiBase.WidgetManager.RemoveAll), PushWidgetToFront/PushWidgetToBack, PushAllTextToFront. - Lookup: GetWidgetByName, GetAllWidgetsByName, GetWidgetByNameAndOwner ← MrxGuiBase.*. - Layout: LoadGuiFile/LoadGUIFile (← MrxGuiBase.LoadGUIFile), UnloadGuiFile, RemoveAllWidgets/RemoveAllWidgetsInLayout, DeleteTransientWidgets, ReAddAllWidgets, HideAllWidgets, ShowAllWidgets, SetAllWidgetsSleep, AssignLayoutToPlayer, DuplicateLayout. - Dialog/numeric: DisplayDialogBox ← MrxGuiDialogBox.DisplayDialogBox, CloseDialogBox ← MrxGuiDialogBox.Close, DisplayNumericBox ← MrxGuiNumericBox.DisplayNumericBox. - Input constants: Joystick ← MrxGuiBase.Joystick (the button-id table other modules read). - Event dispatch: SendEvent ← MrxGuiBase.SentEvent (note the source's SentEvent spelling).

GetObjectiveDescription.doc: Retrieves the description of an objective using a callback function if available. Returns nil if no callback is set or if the input is invalid.

SetObjectiveInformationCallback.doc: Sets a callback function to provide objective information. The callback data can be a table that will be stored and passed back when the callback is invoked.

RemoveObjectiveInformation.doc: Removes an objective from the list of tracked objectives in the callback data.

GlobalFadeToBlack.doc: Initiates a global fade to black effect. If multiple fades are requested simultaneously, they are queued and executed sequentially.

GlobalFadeFromBlack.doc: Completes the global fade from black effect by cleaning up resources and resetting internal state.
GlobalFadeFromBlack.gotcha: Confirmed in source: this function guards if _oTimerEvent then Event.Delete(_oTimerEvent) ... end, but _oTimerEvent is declared nil at module scope (line 84 of source) and is never assigned anywhere else in the file — no Event.Create call in this module ever sets it.

HandleLoadingHint.doc: Handles the display of loading hints during the fade effect by updating the text in the flash widget.

_FinishFadeToBlack.doc: Finishes the fade to black process by setting up event handlers and preparing for the next phase of the fade effect.

_FinishFadeFromBlack.doc: Finishes the fade from black process by pausing the animation, hiding the widget, and cleaning up resources.

_InitFadeFlash.doc: Initializes the flash widget used for global fades. Sets up event handlers and adds the widget to the GUI system.

CleanupFadeFlash.doc: Cleans up the fade flash widget by deleting it and resetting related state.

_CompleteFadeFlashLoad.doc: Completes the loading of the fade flash SWF file, sets up necessary event handlers, and starts the fade effect if queued.

_FadeUpdate.doc: Processes any queued callbacks after a fade update event.

SetGlobalFadeVisible.doc: Sets the visibility of the global fade widget.

FadeToColor.doc: Initiates a color-based fade effect for either the global screen or a specific player's screen. The function handles setting up the animation points and starting the fade process.
FadeToColor.sig: MrxGui.FadeToColor(nTime, uPlayerGuid, nRed, nGreen, nBlue, nAlpha)

FadeFromColor.doc: Completes a color-based fade effect by animating the widget back to full transparency and hiding it when done.

SetFadeEnabled.doc: Enables or disables the global screen fade widget based on the provided boolean flag.

_HideWhenDone.doc: Hides the widget after an animation completes.

AddMessage.doc: Adds a message to the HUD. The function accepts various parameters such as text, priority, duration, and type of message.

ClearMessages.doc: Clears all messages from the HUD.

SetE3HudMode.doc: Toggles the E3/HUD mode on or off. This mode is used for demonstration purposes and can affect how certain UI elements are displayed.

IsE3HudModeActive.doc: Returns a boolean indicating whether the E3/HUD mode is currently active.

FindShellWidget.doc: Finds and returns the ID of the shell widget, which is often used as a base for other GUI elements.

GetReticleSize.doc: Retrieves the size of the reticle image for a given player. If the reticle widget is not found, it defaults to a size of 48.

DisplayDialogBox.doc: Facade alias, not defined in mrxgui.lua: MrxGui.Init() assigns this name to MrxGuiDialogBox.DisplayDialogBox, which opens a modal dialog box. Calling MrxGui.DisplayDialogBox(...) and MrxGuiDialogBox.DisplayDialogBox(...) runs the same code.
DisplayDialogBox.sig: MrxGui.DisplayDialogBox(uPlayerGuid, sMessage, tOptions, nDefaultCursorIndex, fCallback, tCallbackArgs, nXOffset, nYOffset, sHorizAnchor, sVertAnchor, bPause, nCancelOption)
DisplayDialogBox.gotcha: Before MrxGui.Init() has run this name is literally the number 0, not a function - nothing in the MrxGui namespace works until the GUI bootstrap has called Init().

CloseDialogBox.doc: Facade alias, not defined in mrxgui.lua: MrxGui.Init() assigns this name to MrxGuiDialogBox.Close, which closes the currently open dialog box. Calling MrxGui.CloseDialogBox(...) and MrxGuiDialogBox.Close(...) runs the same code.
CloseDialogBox.gotcha: Before MrxGui.Init() has run this name is literally the number 0, not a function - nothing in the MrxGui namespace works until the GUI bootstrap has called Init().

MrxGuiBase.doc: Foundational GUI layer: the Widget/ImageWidget/TextWidget/FlashWidget/SpriteWidget/MovieWidget/MinimapWidget classes plus the WidgetManager that adds, removes, hides, layers and re-adds them, and the control-focus, layout-file and screen-resolution machinery. Most mods reach it indirectly through the MrxGui facade, which re-exports these same functions. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiBase") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiBase' (a nil value)".

GetControlFocus.doc: Manages the focus queue for a given widget. If bPause is true, it sets the dialog box mode; otherwise, it sets the support menu mode.

ReleaseControlFocus.doc: Removes a widget from the control focus queue and updates the control mode accordingly. Called by MrxGuiDialogBox.Close/_CloseAndCallCallback to hand control back when a dialog closes.

GetCurrentControlHolder.doc: Returns the current widget holding control for a given owner GUID or "global".

InformControlOwnerChanged.doc: Placeholder function that currently does nothing.

IsPlayerLocal.doc: Checks if a player is local. Returns true if the player GUID is nil, not in multiplayer, or if the viewport ID is 1.

IsViewportLocal.doc: Checks if a viewport is local. Returns true if the viewport ID is nil, not in multiplayer, or if the viewport ID is 1.

SentEvent.doc: Sends an event to the EventManager.

ProcessEventImmediate.doc: Processes an event immediately based on its type.

AddWidget.doc: Adds a widget to the WidgetManager so it actually renders - the call that makes a hand-built ImageWidget/TextWidget appear on screen.
AddWidget.gotcha: It is declared as a literal = 0 in the decompiled source and never visibly reassigned, which makes it look uncallable; it demonstrably works at runtime, and is normally reached through the MrxGui facade rather than this module directly.

AddWidgetWithChildren.doc: Adds a widget and all its children to the WidgetManager.

RemoveWidget.doc: Removes a widget from the WidgetManager.

RemoveWidgetWithChildren.doc: Removes a widget and all its children from the WidgetManager.

PushAllTextToFront.doc: Pushes all text widgets to the front.

PushWidgetToFront.doc: Pushes a specific widget to the front.

PushWidgetToBack.doc: Pushes a specific widget to the back.

GetWidgetByName.doc: Retrieves a widget by its name.

GetAllWidgetsByName.doc: Retrieves all widgets with a given name.

GetWidgetByNameAndOwner.doc: Retrieves a widget by its name and owner GUID.

DeleteTransientWidgets.doc: Deletes all transient widgets owned by a specific player.

_HandleAnimationComplete.doc: Handles the completion of an animation by calling the completion callback, managing the animation queue, and initiating the next animation point.

_FlashCallback.doc: A helper function that processes callbacks from the flash widget. It unpacks callback data and calls the provided function with the appropriate arguments.

_HandleInputForFlashWidget.doc: Handles input events for Flash widgets. It iterates through the event table and sends corresponding input to the widget based on whether the key contains "ButtonPress" or "ButtonReleased".

MinimapDataUpdateHandler.doc: Handles data updates for the minimap. It updates the minimap's position and rotation, adjusts the range based on player velocity, and corrects widget resolution.

MinimapHandleE3HudModeEvent.doc: Handles E3 HUD mode events by setting the visibility of the minimap based on whether the event is "on" or "off".

LoadGUIFile.doc: Loads a GUI file dynamically. It sets up a callback that calls GUIFileLoadedCallback and an optional finished loading callback.

RemoveAllWidgetsInLayout.doc: Removes all widgets in a given module by iterating through the AddedWidgetList and calling RemoveWidgetWithChildren.

ReAddAllWidgets.doc: Re-adds all widgets in a given module by iterating through the AddedWidgetList and calling AddWidgetWithChildren.

HideAllWidgets.doc: Hides all widgets in a given module by setting their visibility to false.

ShowAllWidgets.doc: Shows all widgets in a given module by setting their visibility to true.

SetAllWidgetsSleep.doc: Sets the sleeping state for all widgets in a given module.

AssignLayoutToPlayer.doc: Assigns a layout to a player by setting the owner GUID for each widget in the module's AddedWidgetList.

DuplicateLayout.doc: Duplicates a GUI layout by creating a new module with a copy of the original's LocalWidgetList. It calls GUIFileLoadedCallback to initialize the new module.

GUIFileLoadedCallback.doc: Handles the loading of a GUI file. It initializes the AddedWidgetList, loads and adds widgets from the LocalWidgetList, triggers any initialization events, and corrects widget resolution for each widget.

LoadAndAddWidgetFromLayoutFileData.doc: This function creates and adds a new widget to the GUI based on the provided layout data. It handles different types of widgets such as images, text, minimaps, flash, and sprite widgets.

UnloadGUIFile.doc: This function unloads a GUI file by calling dynamic_remove with the provided file.

ChangeScreenResolution.doc: This function changes the screen resolution and updates the screen dimensions and scale factor accordingly. It also marks all widgets as needing correction for the new resolution.
ChangeScreenResolution.sig: MrxGuiBase.ChangeScreenResolution(nWidth, nHeight, nNewPixelWidth, nNewPixelHeight, nX, nY)

ChangeScreenPixelSize.doc: This function changes the pixel size of the screen and updates the pixel width and height accordingly.

ValidateParameter.doc: This function validates a parameter against a specified type. If the parameter matches the type, it returns the parameter; otherwise, it returns a default value.

Run.doc: This function processes events using EventManager.ProcessEvents.

GetEventListTable.doc: This function returns the event list table from EventManager.EventList.

SetDialogBoxMode.doc: This function sets the dialog box mode for a player. It checks if the provided parameters are of the correct types and then calls _SetDialogBoxMode with the player GUID and activation status.

SetSupportMenuMode.doc: This function sets the support menu mode for a player. It checks if the provided parameters are of the correct types and then calls _SetSupportMenuMode with the player GUID and activation status.

Init.doc: This function initializes various widget types (TextWidget, ImageWidget, FlashWidget, MinimapWidget, SpriteWidget, MovieWidget) and sets their transient properties to nil. It also adjusts joystick button mappings if necessary.

ReInit.doc: This function is intended for reinitializing the GUI but currently does nothing.

DeInit.doc: This function is intended for deinitializing the GUI but currently does nothing.

_SetDialogBoxMode.doc: Captured reference to the engine global GuiSetDialogBoxMode, stashed at module load (the global is then cleared out of _G). The public SetDialogBoxMode type-checks its arguments and delegates here.
_SetDialogBoxMode.gotcha: Call the public SetDialogBoxMode instead; it returns false rather than erroring if the engine never provided GuiSetDialogBoxMode or if the arguments are the wrong types.

_SetSupportMenuMode.doc: Captured reference to the engine global GuiSetSupportMenuMode, stashed at module load (the global is then cleared out of _G). The public SetSupportMenuMode type-checks its arguments and delegates here.
_SetSupportMenuMode.gotcha: Call the public SetSupportMenuMode instead; it returns false rather than erroring if the engine never provided GuiSetSupportMenuMode or if the arguments are the wrong types.

MrxGuiHudMessage.doc: Drives on-screen messages and fanfares: full-screen contract/mission/wager payout fanfares, 'new contact / new shop item / new landing zone' unlock pop-ups, business-card reveals, COMPLETED/FAILED stamps, sliding text fanfares and the 'classy text' effect. Fanfares are mostly Scaleform FlashWidgets driven through ActionScript callbacks. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiHudMessage") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiHudMessage' (a nil value)".

CreateFanfare.doc: Creates a new fanfare widget based on the specified type (contract, mission, wager, support, contact, or card) and faction. It initializes the widget with necessary properties and sets up event handlers for input and loading completion.

SetFanfareCompleteCallback.doc: Sets a callback function that will be called when the fanfare completes. The callback can include additional data passed through tCallbackData.

SupportFanfareAddItem.doc: Adds an item to the support fanfare widget with specified texture and details. This function is used to populate the items in a support-related fanfare.

SupportFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the support fanfare if it is ready to begin. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare.

_SupportLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the support widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginSupportFanfare.doc: Begins playing the support fanfare by setting its visibility and triggering a scroll-out effect after 3 seconds.

_ScrollOutFanfare.doc: Handles the scroll-out effect of the fanfare, calling an action script callback and scheduling the widget's deletion.

ContactFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the contact fanfare with specified texture and details. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare.

_ContactLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the contact widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginContactFanfare.doc: Begins playing the contact fanfare by setting its visibility and triggering a scroll-out effect after 3 seconds.

CardFanfareSetParameters.doc: Sets parameters for the business card fanfare, including title, name, job title, contact information, and display time. It marks the card as ready if all required fields are provided.
CardFanfareSetParameters.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.CardFanfareSetParameters(sTitle, sName, sJobTitle, sPhone1, sPhone2, sEmail, nDisplayTime)

CardFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the business card fanfare if it is ready to begin. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare and sends network events if applicable.

_CardLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the card widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginCardFanfare.doc: Begins playing the business card fanfare by setting its visibility, calling an action script callback to start the fanfare, and scheduling cleanup events.

_ContinueCardFanfare.doc: Continues the business card fanfare by calling an action script callback and scheduling the end of the fanfare based on the display time.

_EndCardFanfare.doc: Ends the business card fanfare by calling an action script callback to conclude the fanfare.

_CleanupCardFanfare.doc: Cleans up the business card fanfare by scheduling its deletion after a short delay.

SetFanfareParameters.doc: Sets parameters for contract or mission fanfares, including profile names, cancel message, and retry option. It ensures that only valid types are set.

AddFanfareLineItem.doc: Adds a line item to the contract or wager fanfare with specified description, value, type, and player index. It checks for valid input and ensures that the cancel message is not set.

CommenceFanfare.doc: Starts the fanfare by locking HQ, sending network events if applicable, setting up time dilation effects, and preparing the fanfare widget for display. It also handles UI state changes like disabling the HUD and PDA.

NetClientCloseFanfare.doc: Closes the fanfare on the client side by stopping sound callbacks, closing the fanfare, and ending it.

_SlowdownUpdate.doc: Handles the time dilation effect during the fanfare, updating the time scale and fade widget's alpha value accordingly. It triggers the beginning of the fanfare when the time scale reaches zero.

_LoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the main widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginFanfareFlash.doc: This function initializes the fanfare flash sequence for a given widget. It checks if the loading is complete and proceeds to close any pause screens, set invincibility for the local player, initialize the fanfare, create a timer event for an initial delay, and get control focus.

_InitializeFanfareFlash.doc: This function initializes the fanfare flash by setting up various properties of the widget. It changes the shell state, sets visibility and pauses the widget, calls action script callbacks to initialize the fanfare with player data, and sets up event handlers for closing, retrying, and continuing the fanfare.

_ContinueFanfare.doc: This function handles the continuation of the fanfare by calling an action script callback to make the fanfare buttons appear.

_InitialDelay.doc: This function makes the widget visible and plays it after a short delay.

_SkipFanfare.doc: This function sets up event listeners for skipping the fanfare based on player input. It creates events for button presses that trigger the _EndFanfare function.

_RetryEvents.doc: This function sets up persistent event listeners for retrying the fanfare using left stick inputs and selection buttons. It sends flash inputs to handle these actions.

OnPlayerJoined.doc: This function handles the event when a player joins the game. If there is an active fanfare flash widget, it sends a specific input to the widget.

_DeleteFanfareEvents.doc: This function deletes various persistent events related to the fanfare flash sequence.

_EndFanfare.doc: This function ends the fanfare flash by handling cleanup tasks such as deleting events, releasing control focus, and calling callbacks. It also unlocks all HQs if necessary.

_DeleteFanfareWidget.doc: This function deletes the fanfare widget, removes it from the GUI, and calls any callback functions associated with it. It also handles restoring certain game states like PDA suppression and scope enabling.

_HandleFanfareInput.doc: This function handles input events for the fanfare flash by calling a custom handler defined in the widget's custom data.

ShowTextFanfare.doc: This function creates and displays a text-based fanfare with two lines of text. It sets up animations for entering, displaying, and fading out the text, and calls a callback function when the fanfare is done.
ShowTextFanfare.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.ShowTextFanfare(uPlayerGuid, sLine1, sLine2, nEnterTime, nDisplayTime, nFadeTime, fCallback, tCallbackData)

_TextFanfareDone.doc: This function handles the completion of a text fanfare by calling the provided callback function and cleaning up the widget.

_TextDelay.doc: This function sets up a delay before fading out the text in a text fanfare.

_TextFadeout.doc: This function handles the fade-out animation of the text in a text fanfare.

_TextDelete.doc: This function removes and deletes the animated widget from the text fanfare.

ShowEventFanfare.doc: Displays an event fanfare message on the HUD.

_EventFanfareFinishAppear.doc: Handles the appearance animation completion of an event fanfare.

_EventFanfareProcessTextQueue.doc: Processes the text queue for sequential display in the event fanfare.

_EventFanfareContinueTextFade.doc: Continues the fade animation for the next text in the queue.

_EventFanfareFinishDisplay.doc: Handles the display animation completion of an event fanfare.

_EventFanfareComplete.doc: Completes the event fanfare by removing the widget and executing the callback.

GetEventFanfareTitle.doc: Retrieves the title for a given event type.

HandleInitialization.doc: Handles initialization of a widget by setting its translucency and scheduling removal.

ShowCompletedMessage.doc: Displays a completed message on the HUD.

ShowFailedMessage.doc: Displays a failed message on the HUD.

ShowMessage.doc: Displays a message on the HUD with specified parameters.
ShowMessage.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.ShowMessage(uPlayerGuid, sTextureName, fZoomCompleteCallback, fFadeCompleteCallback, nXLocation, nYLocation, sHorizontalAnchor, sVerticalAnchor, nMessageWidth, nMessageHeight, nMessageDisplayTime, vSoundEffect)

AnimationFinishCallback.doc: Handles the completion of an animation for a widget.

HandleUpdateEvent.doc: Updates the display time remaining for a widget and handles removal if necessary.

RemovalCallback.doc: Handles the removal of a widget after its fade animation completes.

Init.doc: Initializes the module by loading necessary fonts.

HandleClassyTextInit.doc: Initializes a widget for displaying classy text.

DisplayClassyText.doc: Displays classy text on the HUD with specified parameters.
DisplayClassyText.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.DisplayClassyText(oWidget, sText, nX, nY, nDuration, nScale, sHorizAnchor, sVertAnchor, sJustification, bExpand)

_ClassyTextLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Handles the completion of loading a classy text widget.

_HandleClassyTextEnd.doc: Handles the end of a classy text widget by scheduling its deletion.

_DeleteClassyText.doc: Deletes a classy text widget from the HUD.

MrxGuiManager.doc: Loads the master HUD, binoculars, satellite and PDA layouts, duplicates them per player, and owns the HUD's sleep/visibility stack. Use it to add or remove your own widget from a player's HUD and to toggle the HUD or satellite overlay. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiManager' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Resets the module's four tracking tables (_tPlayerGuiList, _tPendingList, _tHudStates, _tPendingHudWidgets) to empty. Standard lifecycle reset, not something a mod would normally call directly.

CreateGui.doc: Called when a new player's GUI needs to be created. Loads master copies of GUI layouts if they haven't been loaded yet, then duplicates these layouts for the given player.

ToggleHud.doc: Toggles the visibility state of the HUD for a given player. Uses a refcounted sleep/visibility stack (nHudState) to manage when widgets should be shown or hidden.

_DetoggleWidget.doc: Private function that wakes up a single widget by name and owner.

_DetoggleWidgetRecursive.doc: Private function that recursively wakes up a widget and all its children by name and owner.

_RecursiveWakeup.doc: Private recursive function that sets a widget and all its children to be awake (not sleeping).

GetHudState.doc: Returns the current visibility state of the HUD for a given player.

AddWidgetToHud.doc: Adds a widget to a specific player's HUD, recursing into its children when bIncludeChildren is true. Use it instead of a bare AddWidget when the widget should belong to one player's HUD layout.

RemoveWidgetFromHud.doc: Removes a widget from the HUD for a given player. If the widget has children and bRemoveChildren is true, it recursively removes all children as well.

ToggleSatellite.doc: Toggles the satellite overlay state for a given player. Sets up callbacks for map mode changes and sends events to update the satellite progress and state.
